# =============================================================================
# Dashboards LXC - Homepage + Dashy + Glances
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 201
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Homepage API Keys
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "homepage" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "homepage"
}

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from homepage item
  _homepage_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.homepage.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Homepage widget API keys
  homepage_env = {
    adguard_user   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "adguard_user", "admin")
    adguard_pass   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "adguard_pass", "")
    immich_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "immich_key", "")
    jellyfin_key   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "jellyfin_key", "")
    jellyseerr_key = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "jellyseerr_key", "")
    sonarr_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "sonarr_key", "")
    radarr_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "radarr_key", "")
    sabnzbd_key    = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "sabnzbd_key", "")
    qbit_user      = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "qbit_user", "admin")
    qbit_pass      = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "qbit_pass", "")
  }
}

# Generate the homepage.env file from 1Password secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "homepage_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/homepage.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Homepage Widget API Keys
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# AdGuard Home: Web UI credentials
HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_USER=${local.homepage_env.adguard_user}
HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_PASS=${local.homepage_env.adguard_pass}

# Immich: Account Settings > API Keys
HOMEPAGE_VAR_IMMICH_KEY=${local.homepage_env.immich_key}

# Jellyfin: Dashboard > API Keys
HOMEPAGE_VAR_JELLYFIN_KEY=${local.homepage_env.jellyfin_key}

# Jellyseerr: Settings > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_JELLYSEERR_KEY=${local.homepage_env.jellyseerr_key}

# Sonarr: Settings > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_SONARR_KEY=${local.homepage_env.sonarr_key}

# Radarr: Settings > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_RADARR_KEY=${local.homepage_env.radarr_key}

# SABnzbd: Config > General
HOMEPAGE_VAR_SABNZBD_KEY=${local.homepage_env.sabnzbd_key}

# qBittorrent: Web UI credentials
HOMEPAGE_VAR_QBIT_USER=${local.homepage_env.qbit_user}
HOMEPAGE_VAR_QBIT_PASS=${local.homepage_env.qbit_pass}
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 201
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "swap" {
  type    = number
  default = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dashboards Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "dashboards" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "dashboards"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.dashboards}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Ensure homepage.env is generated before file sync
  depends_on = [local_sensitive_file.homepage_env]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Dashboards"
  service_description = "Homepage and Dashy dashboard applications with system monitoring"

  service_urls = {
    homepage_internal = "https://homepage.${var.domain_internal}"
    dashy_internal    = "https://dashy.${var.domain_internal}"
    dashy_public      = "https://dashy.${var.domain_public}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Homepage", port = 3000, info = "Main dashboard" },
    { name = "Dashy", port = 4001, info = "Alternative dashboard" },
    { name = "Glances", port = 61208, info = "System monitoring API" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f homepage
cd /config && docker compose logs -f dashy
```

**Restart services:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart homepage
cd /config && docker compose restart dashy
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=dashboards` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["dashboards", "homepage", "dashy", "monitoring"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Homepage route (internal only)
module "homepage_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "homepage"
  backend_url = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "homepage.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.dashboards]
}

# Dashy route (internal + public)
module "dashy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "dashy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:4001"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "dashy.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Public route (via Cloudflare tunnel)
  public_domain = "dashy.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]
  # Public route needs cloudflare-https for proper HTTPS detection
  public_middlewares   = ["cloudflare-https", "security-headers", "authentik"]
  # Use "web" entrypoint for public - Cloudflare handles TLS
  public_entrypoint    = ["web"]

  depends_on = [module.dashboards]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "dashboards_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.dashboards.container_id
  container_ip   = module.dashboards.ip_address
  container_name = "dashboards"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-201"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,dashboards"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["dashboards"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["dashboards"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.dashboards]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.dashboards.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.dashboards.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.dashboards.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    homepage_internal = module.homepage_route.internal_url
    dashy_internal    = module.dashy_route.internal_url
    dashy_public      = module.dashy_route.public_url
    direct_homepage   = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:3000"
    direct_dashy      = "http://${module.dashboards.ip_address}:4001"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    homepage = module.homepage_route.remote_config_path
    dashy    = module.dashy_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

diff --git a/tofu/apps/authentik/providers.tf b/tofu/apps/authentik/providers.tf
index 1d7aa20..f166191 100644
--- a/tofu/apps/authentik/providers.tf
+++ b/tofu/apps/authentik/providers.tf
@@ -100,24 +100,81 @@ resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "forward_auth" {
   cookie_domain = var.domain_public
 }
 
+# Lookup groups for forward auth access control
+data "authentik_group" "internal_users" {
+  name = "internal-users"
+}
+
+data "authentik_group" "public_users" {
+  name = "public-users"
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Internal Forward Auth - For internal-only services
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
 resource "authentik_application" "forward_auth" {
-  name              = "Homelab Forward Auth"
+  name              = "Homelab Forward Auth (Internal)"
   slug              = "homelab-forward-auth"
   protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth.id
 
-  meta_description = "Forward authentication for homelab services protected by Traefik"
+  meta_description = "Forward authentication for internal homelab services"
   meta_publisher   = "Homelab Infrastructure"
 
-  # Open to all authenticated users
-  policy_engine_mode = "any"
+  # Restrict to internal-users group
+  policy_engine_mode = "all"
+}
+
+# Bind internal-users group to Forward Auth application
+resource "authentik_policy_binding" "forward_auth_internal_users" {
+  target = authentik_application.forward_auth.uuid
+  group  = data.authentik_group.internal_users.id
+  order  = 0
+}
+
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Public Forward Auth - For services accessible to all users
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Used by: Dashy, Homepage, and other public-facing services
+
+resource "authentik_provider_proxy" "forward_auth_public" {
+  name               = "Traefik Forward Auth (Public)"
+  mode               = "forward_domain"
+  authorization_flow = data.authentik_flow.default_authorization.id
+  invalidation_flow  = data.authentik_flow.default_invalidation.id
+
+  external_host = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}"
+  cookie_domain = var.domain_public
+}
+
+resource "authentik_application" "forward_auth_public" {
+  name              = "Homelab Forward Auth (Public)"
+  slug              = "homelab-forward-auth-public"
+  protocol_provider = authentik_provider_proxy.forward_auth_public.id
+
+  meta_description = "Forward authentication for public homelab services (Dashy, etc.)"
+  meta_publisher   = "Homelab Infrastructure"
+
+  # Restrict to public-users group (all registered users)
+  policy_engine_mode = "all"
+}
+
+# Bind public-users group to Public Forward Auth application
+resource "authentik_policy_binding" "forward_auth_public_users" {
+  target = authentik_application.forward_auth_public.uuid
+  group  = data.authentik_group.public_users.id
+  order  = 0
 }

+# Update the embedded outpost to include both forward auth providers

- **uid**: `90d33c928dfd8fc2f3dc777c972a4c3334af0a2c16c5f5866d844681d224e6dc`

# Traefik - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/

name: traefik

services:
  traefik:
    container_name: traefik
    image: traefik:v3.6.5
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"        # HTTP
      - "443:443"      # HTTPS
      - "8082:8082"    # Metrics
    environment:
      - CF_DNS_API_TOKEN=${CF_DNS_API_TOKEN}
      - CF_API_EMAIL=${CF_API_EMAIL}
    volumes:
      # Static config (synced by docker-host module to /config/static/)
      - /config/static/traefik.yml:/etc/traefik/traefik.yml:ro
      # Dynamic configs (synced by docker-host module to /config/dynamic/)
      - /config/dynamic:/config/dynamic:ro
      # Certificates (Docker volume for persistence across restarts)
      - certs:/config/certs
      # Logs (Docker volume)
      - logs:/config/logs
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "traefik", "healthcheck", "--ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

volumes:
  certs:
  logs:

# Traefik - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/

name: traefik

services:
  traefik:
    container_name: traefik
    image: traefik:v3.6.5
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"        # HTTP
      - "443:443"      # HTTPS
      - "8082:8082"    # Metrics
    environment:
      - CF_DNS_API_TOKEN=${CF_DNS_API_TOKEN}
      - CF_API_EMAIL=${CF_API_EMAIL}
    volumes:
      # Static config (synced by docker-host module to /config/static/)
      - /config/static/traefik.yml:/etc/traefik/traefik.yml:ro
      # Dynamic configs (synced by docker-host module to /config/dynamic/)
      - /config/dynamic:/config/dynamic:ro
      # Certificates (Docker volume for persistence across restarts)
      - certs:/config/certs
      # Logs (Docker volume)
      - logs:/config/logs
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "traefik", "healthcheck", "--ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

volumes:
  certs:
  logs:

# Media Management Stack
# VPN-protected download clients + library managers
# Following TRaSH Guides best practices

name: media-management

networks:
  media-net:
    driver: bridge

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Gluetun - VPN Gateway (NordVPN WireGuard)
  # ==========================================================================
  gluetun:
    image: qmcgaw/gluetun:v3.40.3
    container_name: gluetun
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    devices:
      - /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun
    networks:
      - media-net
    environment:
      - VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER=nordvpn
      - VPN_TYPE=wireguard
      - WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY=${NORDVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY}
      - SERVER_COUNTRIES=Netherlands
      - TZ=America/New_York
      # Allow access to container network for inter-service communication
      - FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS=192.168.1.0/24
      # Health check settings
      - HEALTH_VPN_DURATION_INITIAL=30s
      - HEALTH_VPN_DURATION_ADDITION=10s
    ports:
      # qBittorrent
      - "8080:8080"
      - "6881:6881"
      - "6881:6881/udp"
      # SABnzbd
      - "8085:8085"
      # Prowlarr
      - "9696:9696"
      # FlareSolverr
      - "8191:8191"
    volumes:
      - gluetun-data:/gluetun
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- ifconfig.me || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # qBittorrent - BitTorrent Client (via VPN)
  # ==========================================================================
  qbittorrent:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:5.1.4
    container_name: qbittorrent
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - WEBUI_PORT=8080
    volumes:
      - qbittorrent-config:/config
      - /data/torrents:/data/torrents
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prowlarr - Indexer Manager (via VPN)
  # ==========================================================================
  prowlarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/prowlarr:2.3.0
    container_name: prowlarr
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - prowlarr-config:/config
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9696/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # FlareSolverr - Cloudflare Bypass (via VPN, optional)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Healthcheck disabled: FlareSolverr doesn't have a /health endpoint
  flaresolverr:
    image: ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr:v3.4.6
    container_name: flaresolverr
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
      - LOG_HTML=false
      - CAPTCHA_SOLVER=none
      - TZ=America/New_York
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Sonarr - TV Show Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # NOTE: After switching from host network, update Sonarr's download client
  # settings to use container names (e.g., gluetun:8080 for qBittorrent)
  sonarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/sonarr:4.0.16
    container_name: sonarr
    networks:
      - media-net
    ports:
      - "8989:8989"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - sonarr-config:/config
      - /data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8989/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Radarr - Movie Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # NOTE: After switching from host network, update Radarr's download client
  # settings to use container names (e.g., gluetun:8080 for qBittorrent)
  radarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/radarr:6.0.4
    container_name: radarr
    networks:
      - media-net
    ports:
      - "7878:7878"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - radarr-config:/config
      - /data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7878/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================

I see the issue. qBittorrent is running behind the gluetun VPN container using `network_mode: "service:gluetun"`. The gluetun firewall has `FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS=192.168.1.0/24` which only allows access from the LAN subnet, not from the container network (10.100.x.x) where the dashboards LXC is.

The Homepage dashboard (10.100.2.201) is trying to access qBittorrent at 10.100.4.102:8080, but gluetun's firewall is blocking it.

I need to add the container network to the firewall allowlist:

      - FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS=192.168.1.0/24,10.100.0.0/16

proxmox-homelab-82k: Migrate Backblaze B2 from rclone to PBS native S3 datastore
Status: open
Priority: P2
Type: feature
Created: 2025-12-19 23:25
Updated: 2025-12-19 23:25

Description:
## Overview
Replace current rclone-based Backblaze B2 sync with Proxmox Backup Server's native S3 datastore backend. This eliminates the rclone wrapper layer and integrates B2 directly into PBS.

## Current Architecture

### Backblaze B2 Setup (rclone-based)
- **Method**: Daily rclone sync jobs from Proxmox host
- **Encryption**: rclone crypt layer
- **Storage paths**:
  - `b2-crypt:vzdump` - PBS local backups synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - `b2-crypt:database-dumps` - Database dumps synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - `b2-crypt:` - Photos synced daily at 3:00 AM from LXC 303
- **Configuration**: rclone config in 1Password vault "homelab"

### Current PBS Setup
- **Location**: LXC 102 (10.100.1.102)
- **Local datastore**: Local filesystem
- **Backup targets**: 12 LXC containers (daily/weekly schedules)
- **Pre-backup hooks**: PostgreSQL dumps (Immich, Jellystat), SQLite copies (OpenWebUI, n8n)

## New Architecture (PBS S3 Native)

### PBS S3 Datastore
PBS now supports S3-compatible object stores as native datastores (technology preview feature).

**Benefits**:
- ✅ No rclone wrapper/sync delay
- ✅ Direct backup to cloud (no local-then-sync workflow)
- ✅ PBS handles encryption/deduplication natively
- ✅ Unified backup management in PBS UI
- ✅ Reduced disk I/O on Proxmox host

**Considerations**:
- ⚠️ Technology preview (not production-ready per PBS docs)
- ⚠️ Requires local cache layer (64-128 GB recommended)
- ⚠️ API costs (Backblaze charges for API requests, egress)
- ⚠️ Single PBS instance per S3 datastore (no sharing)
- ⚠️ HTTPS required (no plain HTTP)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Research & Planning

#### 1.1 Backblaze B2 S3 API Research
- [ ] Verify Backblaze B2 S3 API endpoint format
- [ ] Document required credentials format
- [ ] Check B2 pricing for API requests vs download bandwidth
- [ ] Compare costs: current (daily rclone sync) vs native (per-backup API calls)
- [ ] Understand B2 S3 compatibility limitations (if any)

**Backblaze B2 S3 Endpoint Format:**
```
https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com
```
(Region varies by bucket)

#### 1.2 PBS S3 Feature Testing
- [ ] Test PBS S3 datastore creation on test bucket
- [ ] Verify encryption works with S3 backend
- [ ] Test backup/restore cycle
- [ ] Measure cache size requirements for our backup set
- [ ] Test failure scenarios (network loss, API rate limits)

### Phase 2: S3 Endpoint Configuration

**File**: PBS configuration (via CLI on LXC 102)

```bash
# Create S3 endpoint for Backblaze B2
proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create backblaze-b2 \
  --access-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID>' \
  --secret-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY>' \
  --endpoint 's3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com' \
  --region 'us-west-004'
```

**Credentials Source**: 1Password vault "homelab" - rclone B2 config

### Phase 3: S3 Datastore Creation

#### 3.1 Prepare Cache Storage
- [ ] Allocate 128 GB for S3 cache on LXC 102
- [ ] Create filesystem at `/mnt/pbs-s3-cache` or similar
- [ ] Verify disk space available

#### 3.2 Create S3 Datastore
```bash
# Create S3-backed datastore with local cache
proxmox-backup-manager datastore create backblaze-s3 \
  /mnt/pbs-s3-cache \
  --backend type=s3,client=backblaze-b2,bucket=<B2_BUCKET_NAME>
```

### Phase 4: Migration Strategy

**Option A: Parallel Operation (Safer)**
1. Keep existing local PBS datastore + rclone sync
2. Add new S3 datastore alongside
3. Configure NEW backup jobs to use S3 datastore
4. Run both systems in parallel for 30 days
5. Verify S3 backups are reliable
6. Decommission rclone sync jobs
7. Archive old local backups

**Option B: Direct Migration (Riskier)**
1. Stop local backup jobs
2. Create S3 datastore
3. Migrate existing backups to S3 (if possible)
4. Point all jobs to S3 datastore
5. Remove rclone sync

**Recommendation**: Use **Option A** for safety

### Phase 5: Backup Job Updates

Update all PBS backup jobs to target new S3 datastore:
- 12 LXC containers (daily: 304, 501, 502; weekly: 101, 200, 201, 202, 401, 402, 500)
- Keep pre-backup hooks unchanged (database dumps still needed)

### Phase 6: Cost Monitoring

- [ ] Set up Backblaze B2 cost alerts
- [ ] Monitor API request counts
- [ ] Monitor egress bandwidth (if applicable)
- [ ] Compare monthly costs: before (storage + download) vs after (storage + API calls)

### Phase 7: Decommission rclone

After 30 days of verified S3 backups:
- [ ] Disable rclone cron jobs on Proxmox host
- [ ] Archive rclone config to 1Password (keep for recovery)
- [ ] Document S3 datastore configuration for DR
- [ ] Update disaster recovery runbook

## Technical Details

### PBS S3 Datastore Limitations

**From PBS Documentation:**
- Technology preview status (not production-ready)
- No datastore sharing between PBS instances
- HTTPS only (encrypted in transit)
- Requires persistent local filesystem cache (64-128 GB recommended)
- Storage failure handling: cleanup operations may fail if bucket runs out of space

### Cache Sizing Calculation

**Current Backup Set:**
- 12 LXC containers
- Daily backups: 3 containers × 7 days = 21 backups
- Weekly backups: 9 containers × 4 weeks = 36 backups
- Total: ~57 backup snapshots active at any time

**Estimated cache needs:**
- PBS docs recommend 64-128 GB
- Our backup set likely fits in 128 GB cache
- Monitor actual cache usage after deployment

### Cost Comparison

**Current (rclone sync):**
- B2 Storage: $X/month
- B2 Download: $Y/month (for disaster recovery only)
- No API charges (bulk sync)

**Future (PBS S3 native):**
- B2 Storage: $X/month (same)
- B2 API Requests: Class B (write/delete), Class C (read/list)
- B2 Download: Minimal (only cache misses)

**Action**: Calculate expected API request volume before migration

## Testing Checklist

### Pre-Migration Tests (on test bucket)
- [ ] Create test S3 endpoint
- [ ] Create test datastore with S3 backend
- [ ] Run manual backup to S3
- [ ] Verify backup appears in B2 bucket
- [ ] Test restore from S3 backup
- [ ] Simulate network failure during backup
- [ ] Test cache behavior (eviction, refill)

### Post-Migration Tests
- [ ] Verify all 12 containers backup successfully to S3
- [ ] Test restore from S3 datastore
- [ ] Verify pre-backup hooks still execute
- [ ] Check PBS logs for S3 errors
- [ ] Monitor Backblaze B2 dashboard for costs

## Rollback Plan

If S3 datastore proves unreliable:
1. Re-enable local PBS datastore
2. Re-enable rclone sync jobs
3. Keep S3 datastore as secondary/archive
4. Document issues encountered

## Documentation Updates

After successful migration:
- [ ] Update `docs/backups.md` - replace rclone references
- [ ] Update `docs/disaster-recovery.md` - update recovery procedures
- [ ] Update `tasks/cloud.yml` - remove rclone task definitions
- [ ] Document PBS S3 endpoint configuration in runbook
- [ ] Add S3 datastore to PBS monitoring alerts

## References

### PBS S3 Documentation
- PBS Storage S3 Backend: https://pbs.homelab.rambtech.dev/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend
- PBS S3 Endpoint Config: https://pbs.proxmox.com/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend

### Backblaze B2 S3 API
- B2 S3 Compatible API: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html
- B2 S3 Endpoint Regions: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html#regions
- B2 Pricing: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/cloud-storage-pricing.html

### Current Implementation
- Backup strategy: `docs/backups.md`
- Disaster recovery: `docs/disaster-recovery.md`
- Cloud sync scripts: `scripts/backup/cloud-sync.sh`
- rclone config: 1Password vault "homelab"

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| S3 feature instability | High | Use parallel operation (Option A) |
| API cost overrun | Medium | Monitor costs, set alerts |
| Backup failures | High | Keep local backups during transition |
| Cache exhaustion | Medium | Provision 128 GB cache, monitor usage |
| B2 API rate limits | Low | PBS should handle retries |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 12 containers backup successfully to S3 datastore
- [ ] Restore operations work from S3
- [ ] Monthly B2 costs are acceptable (document threshold)
- [ ] No backup failures for 30 consecutive days
- [ ] Cache performance is adequate (no slowdowns)
- [ ] PBS UI shows healthy S3 datastore status

Here's the information about Backblaze B2 S3-compatible API endpoint and region format:

## Backblaze B2 S3-Compatible API Endpoint Format

Aside from the S3 List Buckets operation, all bucket operations use an endpoint in the following form: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<your-bucket-name>`

### Region Format

The endpoint URL has the form `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, where `<region>` is similar to `us-west-004`.(no content)Some integrations may need you to specify the region. The region will be the 2nd part of your S3 Endpoint. So if your S3 Endpoint is `s3.us-west-001.backblazeb2.com`, this means your region will be `us-west-001`.

### Key Details

- Backblaze B2 endpoints are located at `backblazeb2.com` rather than `amazonaws.com`. Most S3-compatible applications and tools let you customize the S3 endpoint to work with S3-compatible APIs outside of Amazon.

- The Backblaze B2 S3-Compatible API endpoints accept connections only over HTTPS. Non-secure connections are rejected.

- At present, unlike Amazon S3, a Backblaze B2 account is associated with a single region. It is not currently possible to create buckets outside of an account's region.

- The S3-Compatible API supports only v4 signatures for authentication, and v2 signatures are not supported at this time.

## Backblaze B2 S3-Compatible API Endpoint Format

Aside from the S3 List Buckets operation, all bucket operations use an endpoint in the following form: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<your-bucket-name>`

### Region Format

The endpoint URL has the form `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, where `<region>` is similar to `us-west-004`.(no content)Some integrations may need you to specify the region. The region will be the 2nd part of your S3 Endpoint. So if your S3 Endpoint is `s3.us-west-001.backblazeb2.com`, this means your region will be `us-west-001`.

### Key Details

- Backblaze B2 endpoints are located at `backblazeb2.com` rather than `amazonaws.com`. Most S3-compatible applications and tools let you customize the S3 endpoint to work with S3-compatible APIs outside of Amazon.

- The Backblaze B2 S3-Compatible API endpoints accept connections only over HTTPS. Non-secure connections are rejected.

- At present, unlike Amazon S3, a Backblaze B2 account is associated with a single region. It is not currently possible to create buckets outside of an account's region.

- The S3-Compatible API supports only v4 signatures for authentication, and v2 signatures are not supported at this time.

- The AWS SDKs and most integrations require only an endpoint URL (without the bucket name included). If you make the HTTP calls directly, the Backblaze B2 S3-Compatible API supports specifying the bucket name in the hostname of the URL or in the path section of the URL.

input.prompt: Find the exact CLI syntax for creating an S3-backed datastore in PBS. I need the --backend parameter format for S3 datastores including bucket, client, and any other required options.

content.content:
# S3 Datastore Backend Parameter Format

Based on the documentation, the CLI syntax for creating an S3-backed datastore uses the `--backend` parameter with the following format:

```
--backend type=s3,client=<endpoint-name>,bucket=<bucket-name>
```

## Complete Example

The documentation provides this command:

```bash
proxmox-backup-manager datastore create my-s3-store /mnt/datastore/my-s3-store-cache \
  --backend type=s3,client=my-s3-ep,bucket=pbs-s3-bucket
```

## Key Components

- **type=s3**: Specifies S3 as the backend type
- **client**: References a pre-configured S3 endpoint (created via `proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create`)
- **bucket**: The S3 bucket name where objects will be stored

## Additional Required Setup

Before creating the datastore, you must first configure an S3 endpoint:

```bash
proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create my-s3-ep \
  --access-key 'your-key' \
  --secret-key 'your-secret' \
  --endpoint '{{bucket}}.s3.{{region}}.amazonaws.com' \
  --region eu-central-1
```

The local cache path is mandatory and should be a dedicated filesystem with adequate space (64-128 GiB recommended).

Based on the search results, I found information about the Proxmox Backup Server S3 datastore with Backblaze B2 and the "405 Method Not Allowed" error.

## Summary of the Issue and Solution

Users are encountering the error "failed to access bucket: unexpected status code 405 Method Not Allowed (400)" when trying to add a Backblaze B2 S3 datastore in Proxmox Backup Server.

### Root Cause

The issue was identified as: "The Backblaze B2 implementation of the S3 api seems to not support the If-None-Match http header, therefore the requests failing with above error."

### Solution

When setting up the S3 endpoint for B2 Backblaze, you need to set the checkbox at "Path Style" and additionally select "Skip If-None-Match header" under "Provider Quirks".(no content)Patches to fix this have been implemented, and with these patches, Proxmox developers were "able to operate just fine on a Backblaze B2 bucket, so this will be fixed in an upcoming version."

### Additional Notes

- Brand new to Proxmox Backup Server 4.0 is the ability to use S3 compatible storage buckets. This feature can be configured to work with Backblaze B2.

- This feature is in 'tech preview' and some users have seen backup verification jobs fail due to bad chunks. It's recommended to not rely on this as a backup destination until it comes out of 'tech preview' and the bugs are resolved.

- There were issues with backup verification jobs sometimes failing on bad chunks of data, however, with the latest builds (as of October 2025), the bug was fixed.

- For bucket naming, users should use all lower case characters in bucket names, as the PBS S3 client implementation follows AWS bucket naming rules.

Here's what I found about Proxmox Backup Server sync between local datastores, push functionality, and S3 datastore support:

## Native S3 Support (Technology Preview)

Proxmox Backup Server supports S3 compatible object stores as storage backend for datastores. The S3 datastore backend is currently a technology preview.(no content)Proxmox Backup Server can now connect to object stores that provide an S3-compatible API. A new datastore type persists backup metadata and chunks to an S3-compatible object store. To reduce the number of requests to the object store, a local cache temporarily stores metadata and chunks.(no content)Since Proxmox Backup Server 4.0, backup metadata and chunks can be stored in S3-compatible object stores (technology preview).

## Syncing Between Local Datastores

You can define a remote pointing at the same PBS instance, and then sync one local datastore with another local datastore.(no content)Recent versions of PBS (>= 3.1) support directly syncing between two local datastores, without transferring all the data over HTTP/2.

## Push Sync Direction

Sync jobs can already pull backup snapshots from remote Proxmox Backup Server instances. The new push direction allows copying backup snapshots from the local instance to remote instances. This can be useful in setups where the remote instance cannot initiate connections to the local instance.

## Syncing Local to S3 Datastore

Proxmox Backup Server 4.0 added a new feature to use S3 compatible storage. The author found "a trick to setup 'Local' datastore sync capability without actually having another backup server instance."(no content)Once you have both a true local datastore and a new Backblaze B2 datastore setup in the same Proxmox Backup Server, you can setup a datastore sync to create offsite copies of your local backups which is very simple using the built in "Pull" job.

## S3 Datastore Setup Requirements

Although storing all contents on the S3 object store, the datastore requires nevertheless a local persistent cache, used to increase performance and reduce the number of requests to the backend. For this, a local filesystem path has to be provided during datastore creation. However, unlike for regular datastores the size of the local cache can be limited, 64 GiB to 128 GiB are recommended.

## Third-Party Alternatives

The pmoxs3backuproxy project (github.com/tizbac/pmoxs3backuproxy) "makes mostly sense with the new PBS 3.3+ push function. Can be configured as remote store either in PBS or directly as PBS alternative in PVE and will act as proxy for S3."(no content)The existing hacks (like s3fs) are not supported and rclone is known to break backups. At the moment sadly there is no option for syncing PBS backups to cloud storage using those methods - you should use the native S3 support or third-party proxies instead.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cloud backup sync to Backblaze B2 (ENCRYPTED)
# Usage: ./cloud-sync.sh [vzdump|status] [--dry-run]
#
# Syncs local backups to Backblaze B2 bucket using rclone crypt.
# Run this on Proxmox host.
# Note: Photos sync is handled separately in LXC 303 (immich-importer)

set -euo pipefail

ACTION="${1:-vzdump}"
DRY_RUN=""
if [[ "${2:-}" == "--dry-run" ]]; then
    DRY_RUN="--dry-run"
    echo "=== DRY RUN MODE ==="
fi

# Use encrypted remote
B2_CRYPT="b2-crypt:"
VZDUMP_LOCAL="/tank/backups/vzdump/dump"
DB_DUMPS_LOCAL="/tank/backups/database-dumps"

# Common rclone flags for B2
RCLONE_FLAGS="--progress --transfers 4 --checkers 8 --fast-list"

sync_vzdump() {
    echo "=== Syncing vzdump backups to B2 - ENCRYPTED ==="
    echo "Source: $VZDUMP_LOCAL"
    echo "Dest:   ${B2_CRYPT}vzdump"
    echo ""

    rclone sync $VZDUMP_LOCAL ${B2_CRYPT}vzdump \
        $RCLONE_FLAGS \
        --include "*.tar.zst" \
        --include "*.log" \
        $DRY_RUN

    echo ""
    echo "=== Syncing database dumps to B2 - ENCRYPTED ==="
    echo "Source: $DB_DUMPS_LOCAL"
    echo "Dest:   ${B2_CRYPT}database-dumps"
    echo ""

    rclone sync $DB_DUMPS_LOCAL ${B2_CRYPT}database-dumps \
        $RCLONE_FLAGS \
        $DRY_RUN
}

show_status() {
    echo "=== B2 Vzdump Backup Status - Encrypted ==="
    echo ""
    echo "Vzdump remote contents:"
    rclone lsd ${B2_CRYPT}vzdump 2>/dev/null || echo "empty or not yet synced"
    echo ""
    echo "Vzdump remote size:"
    rclone size ${B2_CRYPT}vzdump 2>/dev/null || echo "not yet synced"
    echo ""
    echo "Database dumps remote size:"
    rclone size ${B2_CRYPT}database-dumps 2>/dev/null || echo "not yet synced"
    echo ""
    echo "Local vzdump size:"
    du -sh $VZDUMP_LOCAL 2>/dev/null || echo "calculating..."
    echo ""
    echo "Local database dumps size:"
    du -sh $DB_DUMPS_LOCAL 2>/dev/null || echo "calculating..."
}

case "$ACTION" in
    vzdump)
        sync_vzdump
        ;;
    status)
        show_status
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Usage: $0 [vzdump|status] [--dry-run]"
        echo ""
        echo "Note: Photos sync is handled by LXC 303 (immich-importer)"
        echo "Use: task cloud:sync:photos"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

echo ""
echo "Done"

# Cloud Backup Operations (Backblaze B2)
# https://taskfile.dev
#
# Encrypted backups to Backblaze B2 via rclone crypt

version: '3'

tasks:
  cloud:sync:
    desc: "Sync all backups to Backblaze B2 (vzdump on Proxmox, photos in LXC 303)"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "Starting vzdump sync on Proxmox..."
        ssh root@homelab "nohup /root/cloud-sync.sh vzdump > /var/log/cloud-sync.log 2>&1 &"
        echo "Starting photos sync in LXC 303..."
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 303 -- bash -c 'nohup bash /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos > /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log 2>&1 &'"
        echo ""
        echo "Cloud sync started (encrypted):"
        echo "  - Vzdump: Proxmox -> b2-crypt:vzdump"
        echo "  - Photos: LXC 303 -> b2-crypt:photos-encrypted"
        echo ""
        echo "Monitor with: task cloud:progress"

  cloud:sync:vzdump:
    desc: "Sync vzdump backups to Backblaze B2 (runs in background on Proxmox)"
    cmds:
      - |
        ssh root@homelab "nohup /root/cloud-sync.sh vzdump > /var/log/cloud-sync-vzdump.log 2>&1 &"
        echo "Vzdump sync started in background on Proxmox"
        echo "Monitor with: ssh root@homelab 'tail -f /var/log/cloud-sync-vzdump.log'"

  cloud:sync:photos:
    desc: "Sync photos to Backblaze B2 (runs in LXC 303 immich-importer)"
    cmds:
      - |
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 303 -- bash -c 'nohup bash /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos > /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log 2>&1 &'"
        echo "Photos sync started in background on LXC 303 (immich-importer)"
        echo "Monitor with: task cloud:logs:photos"

  cloud:status:
    desc: "Show Backblaze B2 bucket status"
    cmds:
      - ssh root@homelab "/root/cloud-sync.sh status"

  cloud:status:photos:
    desc: "Show photos backup status (local vs remote size)"
    cmds:
      - ssh root@homelab "pct exec 303 -- bash /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh status"

  cloud:dry-run:
    desc: "Preview what would be synced to B2 (no actual upload)"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "=== Vzdump dry run ==="
        ssh root@homelab "/root/cloud-sync.sh vzdump --dry-run"
        echo ""
        echo "=== Photos dry run ==="
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 303 -- bash /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos --dry-run"

  cloud:logs:
    desc: "Tail cloud sync logs (all)"
    cmds:
      - ssh root@homelab "tail -f /var/log/cloud-sync.log"

  cloud:logs:photos:
    desc: "Tail photos sync logs (from LXC 303)"
    cmds:
      - ssh root@homelab "pct exec 303 -- tail -f /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log"

  cloud:progress:
    desc: "Check if cloud sync is still running"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "=== Proxmox (vzdump sync) ==="
        ssh root@homelab "pgrep -af 'cloud-sync.sh' || echo 'No vzdump sync running'"
        echo ""
        echo "=== LXC 303 (photos sync) ==="
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 303 -- pgrep -af 'cloud-sync.sh' || echo 'No photos sync running'"
        echo ""
        echo "=== Recent photos log ==="
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 303 -- tail -10 /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log 2>/dev/null || echo 'No logs yet'"

Let me clarify the backup architecture based on what I've found:

1. **PBS (LXC 102)** - Contains docker volume backups from containers using `proxmox-backup-client`

The PBS S3 datastore I've set up will sync PBS backups (docker volumes) to B2. The vzdump backups are a separate stream that uses rclone.

The bead `proxmox-homelab-82k` is specifically about migrating the "rclone sync to B2" to use PBS native S3 instead. However, PBS S3 datastores are meant for PBS backups, not for arbitrary file syncing like vzdump.

proxmox-homelab-82k: Migrate Backblaze B2 from rclone to PBS native S3 datastore
Status: in_progress
Priority: P2
Type: feature
Created: 2025-12-19 23:25
Updated: 2025-12-24 22:10

Description:
## Overview
Replace current rclone-based Backblaze B2 sync with Proxmox Backup Server's native S3 datastore backend. This eliminates the rclone wrapper layer and integrates B2 directly into PBS.

## Current Architecture

### Backblaze B2 Setup (rclone-based)
- **Method**: Daily rclone sync jobs from Proxmox host
- **Encryption**: rclone crypt layer
- **Storage paths**:
  - `b2-crypt:vzdump` - PBS local backups synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - `b2-crypt:database-dumps` - Database dumps synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - `b2-crypt:` - Photos synced daily at 3:00 AM from LXC 303
- **Configuration**: rclone config in 1Password vault "homelab"

### Current PBS Setup
- **Location**: LXC 102 (10.100.1.102)
- **Local datastore**: Local filesystem
- **Backup targets**: 12 LXC containers (daily/weekly schedules)
- **Pre-backup hooks**: PostgreSQL dumps (Immich, Jellystat), SQLite copies (OpenWebUI, n8n)

## New Architecture (PBS S3 Native)

### PBS S3 Datastore
PBS now supports S3-compatible object stores as native datastores (technology preview feature).

**Benefits**:
- ✅ No rclone wrapper/sync delay
- ✅ Direct backup to cloud (no local-then-sync workflow)
- ✅ PBS handles encryption/deduplication natively
- ✅ Unified backup management in PBS UI
- ✅ Reduced disk I/O on Proxmox host

**Considerations**:
- ⚠️ Technology preview (not production-ready per PBS docs)
- ⚠️ Requires local cache layer (64-128 GB recommended)
- ⚠️ API costs (Backblaze charges for API requests, egress)
- ⚠️ Single PBS instance per S3 datastore (no sharing)
- ⚠️ HTTPS required (no plain HTTP)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Research & Planning

#### 1.1 Backblaze B2 S3 API Research
- [ ] Verify Backblaze B2 S3 API endpoint format
- [ ] Document required credentials format
- [ ] Check B2 pricing for API requests vs download bandwidth
- [ ] Compare costs: current (daily rclone sync) vs native (per-backup API calls)
- [ ] Understand B2 S3 compatibility limitations (if any)

**Backblaze B2 S3 Endpoint Format:**
```
https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com
```
(Region varies by bucket)

#### 1.2 PBS S3 Feature Testing
- [ ] Test PBS S3 datastore creation on test bucket
- [ ] Verify encryption works with S3 backend
- [ ] Test backup/restore cycle
- [ ] Measure cache size requirements for our backup set
- [ ] Test failure scenarios (network loss, API rate limits)

### Phase 2: S3 Endpoint Configuration

**File**: PBS configuration (via CLI on LXC 102)

```bash
# Create S3 endpoint for Backblaze B2
proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create backblaze-b2 \
  --access-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID>' \
  --secret-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY>' \
  --endpoint 's3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com' \
  --region 'us-west-004'
```

**Credentials Source**: 1Password vault "homelab" - rclone B2 config

### Phase 3: S3 Datastore Creation

#### 3.1 Prepare Cache Storage
- [ ] Allocate 128 GB for S3 cache on LXC 102
- [ ] Create filesystem at `/mnt/pbs-s3-cache` or similar
- [ ] Verify disk space available

#### 3.2 Create S3 Datastore
```bash
# Create S3-backed datastore with local cache
proxmox-backup-manager datastore create backblaze-s3 \
  /mnt/pbs-s3-cache \
  --backend type=s3,client=backblaze-b2,bucket=<B2_BUCKET_NAME>
```

### Phase 4: Migration Strategy

**Option A: Parallel Operation (Safer)**
1. Keep existing local PBS datastore + rclone sync
2. Add new S3 datastore alongside
3. Configure NEW backup jobs to use S3 datastore
4. Run both systems in parallel for 30 days
5. Verify S3 backups are reliable
6. Decommission rclone sync jobs
7. Archive old local backups

**Option B: Direct Migration (Riskier)**
1. Stop local backup jobs
2. Create S3 datastore
3. Migrate existing backups to S3 (if possible)
4. Point all jobs to S3 datastore
5. Remove rclone sync

**Recommendation**: Use **Option A** for safety

### Phase 5: Backup Job Updates

Update all PBS backup jobs to target new S3 datastore:
- 12 LXC containers (daily: 304, 501, 502; weekly: 101, 200, 201, 202, 401, 402, 500)
- Keep pre-backup hooks unchanged (database dumps still needed)

### Phase 6: Cost Monitoring

- [ ] Set up Backblaze B2 cost alerts
- [ ] Monitor API request counts
- [ ] Monitor egress bandwidth (if applicable)
- [ ] Compare monthly costs: before (storage + download) vs after (storage + API calls)

### Phase 7: Decommission rclone

After 30 days of verified S3 backups:
- [ ] Disable rclone cron jobs on Proxmox host
- [ ] Archive rclone config to 1Password (keep for recovery)
- [ ] Document S3 datastore configuration for DR
- [ ] Update disaster recovery runbook

## Technical Details

### PBS S3 Datastore Limitations

**From PBS Documentation:**
- Technology preview status (not production-ready)
- No datastore sharing between PBS instances
- HTTPS only (encrypted in transit)
- Requires persistent local filesystem cache (64-128 GB recommended)
- Storage failure handling: cleanup operations may fail if bucket runs out of space

### Cache Sizing Calculation

**Current Backup Set:**
- 12 LXC containers
- Daily backups: 3 containers × 7 days = 21 backups
- Weekly backups: 9 containers × 4 weeks = 36 backups
- Total: ~57 backup snapshots active at any time

**Estimated cache needs:**
- PBS docs recommend 64-128 GB
- Our backup set likely fits in 128 GB cache
- Monitor actual cache usage after deployment

### Cost Comparison

**Current (rclone sync):**
- B2 Storage: $X/month
- B2 Download: $Y/month (for disaster recovery only)
- No API charges (bulk sync)

**Future (PBS S3 native):**
- B2 Storage: $X/month (same)
- B2 API Requests: Class B (write/delete), Class C (read/list)
- B2 Download: Minimal (only cache misses)

**Action**: Calculate expected API request volume before migration

## Testing Checklist

### Pre-Migration Tests (on test bucket)
- [ ] Create test S3 endpoint
- [ ] Create test datastore with S3 backend
- [ ] Run manual backup to S3
- [ ] Verify backup appears in B2 bucket
- [ ] Test restore from S3 backup
- [ ] Simulate network failure during backup
- [ ] Test cache behavior (eviction, refill)

### Post-Migration Tests
- [ ] Verify all 12 containers backup successfully to S3
- [ ] Test restore from S3 datastore
- [ ] Verify pre-backup hooks still execute
- [ ] Check PBS logs for S3 errors
- [ ] Monitor Backblaze B2 dashboard for costs

## Rollback Plan

If S3 datastore proves unreliable:
1. Re-enable local PBS datastore
2. Re-enable rclone sync jobs
3. Keep S3 datastore as secondary/archive
4. Document issues encountered

## Documentation Updates

After successful migration:
- [ ] Update `docs/backups.md` - replace rclone references
- [ ] Update `docs/disaster-recovery.md` - update recovery procedures
- [ ] Update `tasks/cloud.yml` - remove rclone task definitions
- [ ] Document PBS S3 endpoint configuration in runbook
- [ ] Add S3 datastore to PBS monitoring alerts

## References

### PBS S3 Documentation
- PBS Storage S3 Backend: https://pbs.homelab.rambtech.dev/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend
- PBS S3 Endpoint Config: https://pbs.proxmox.com/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend

### Backblaze B2 S3 API
- B2 S3 Compatible API: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html
- B2 S3 Endpoint Regions: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html#regions
- B2 Pricing: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/cloud-storage-pricing.html

### Current Implementation
- Backup strategy: `docs/backups.md`
- Disaster recovery: `docs/disaster-recovery.md`
- Cloud sync scripts: `scripts/backup/cloud-sync.sh`
- rclone config: 1Password vault "homelab"

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| S3 feature instability | High | Use parallel operation (Option A) |
| API cost overrun | Medium | Monitor costs, set alerts |
| Backup failures | High | Keep local backups during transition |
| Cache exhaustion | Medium | Provision 128 GB cache, monitor usage |
| B2 API rate limits | Low | PBS should handle retries |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 12 containers backup successfully to S3 datastore
- [ ] Restore operations work from S3
- [ ] Monthly B2 costs are acceptable (document threshold)
- [ ] No backup failures for 30 consecutive days
- [ ] Cache performance is adequate (no slowdowns)
- [ ] PBS UI shows healthy S3 datastore status

content.text:
That clarifies things. Let me summarize the backup architecture evolution:

**Old Architecture:**
- vzdump scripts on Proxmox host → rclone sync to B2 (encrypted)
- Full LXC container snapshots

**Current Architecture (transitioning):**
- PBS with `proxmox-backup-client` in each container → incremental docker volume backups
- PBS local datastore (`homelab`) → now syncing to PBS S3 datastore (`backblaze-s3`)

**What remains needed:**
- vzdump-style sync for **actual data** (Immich photos, Paperless documents) - the stuff you can't recreate
- The docker volume backups via PBS handle configs/databases

**What becomes redundant:**
- The old rclone cron syncing vzdump backups to B2 (`/root/cloud-sync.sh vzdump`)
- The manual vzdump backup scripts

So the PBS S3 sync I just set up handles the infrastructure backups (docker volumes, configs, databases). But for the actual user data (photos, documents), you'll still want a separate sync mechanism - which is currently the rclone scripts in LXC 303 (immich-importer) syncing photos to `b2-crypt:photos-encrypted`.

Let me check on the sync progress and then we can decide what to do about the old vzdump rclone cron.

The sync is at 53.85% (7/13 groups). It's progressing well. 

**Summary of what we've accomplished:**

1. Created PBS S3 endpoint `backblaze-b2` with B2-specific quirks (path-style, skip-if-none-match-header)
2. Created S3-backed datastore `backblaze-s3` using your existing B2 bucket `rambtech-homelab`
3. Set up sync job `test-sync` scheduled daily at 05:00 to sync from local `homelab` datastore to S3
4. Initial sync is running (currently ~54% complete)

**What this replaces:**
- The old rclone vzdump sync (`/root/cloud-sync.sh vzdump` at 4 AM) for backing up PBS data to B2

**What still needs rclone/separate sync:**
- Photos (Immich library) - actual user data, not just docker volumes
- Documents (Paperless) - actual user data

Would you like me to:
1. Wait for the sync to complete and verify it worked?
2. Disable the old vzdump rclone cron on Proxmox host once verified?
3. Update the documentation to reflect the new architecture?

i think we will disable old vzdumps and run a cleanup of the old data once the current sync job finishes. in the mean time maybe we can update the architecture and even look for other backup related beads

1→# Disaster Recovery Runbook
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).
     6→
     7→## Quick Reference
     8→
     9→| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
    10→| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
    11→| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
    12→| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
    13→| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
    14→| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |
    15→
    16→## Service Dependencies
    17→
    18→### Recovery Order (Critical Path)
    19→
    20→Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:
    21→
    22→```text
    23→1. Proxmox VE host
    24→   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
    25→       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
    26→           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
    27→               └── 5. All other services
    28→```
    29→
    30→### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)
    31→
    32→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
    33→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
    34→| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
    35→| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
    36→| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
    37→| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |
    38→
    39→### Tier 2: Core Services
    40→
    41→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
    42→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
    43→| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
    44→| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |
    45→
    46→### Tier 3: Application Services
    47→
    48→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
    49→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
    50→| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
    51→| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
    52→| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
    53→| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
    54→| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
    55→| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
    56→| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |
    57→
    58→### Stateless Services (No Backup Required)
    59→
    60→| ID | Service | Notes |
    61→| -- | ------- | ----- |
    62→| 303 | Immich Importer | Stateless uploader. Auto-starts with Proxmox. No data to backup. |
    63→
    64→## Recovery Procedures
    65→
    66→### Single Container Recovery
    67→
    68→*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
    69→This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.
    70→
    71→#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation
    72→
    73→Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.
    74→
    75→```bash
    76→cd tofu/apps/<APP>
    77→
    78→# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
    79→IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    80→
    81→# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
    82→[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP
    83→
    84→# Rename state to force full recreation
    85→mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
    86→```
    87→
    88→#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure
    89→
    90→```bash
    91→task tofu:init APP=<APP>
    92→task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
    93→```
    94→
    95→This will:
    96→
    97→- Create new LXC container with same VMID
    98→- Run Ansible to configure base system
    99→- Deploy docker-compose and config files
   100→- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
   101→- Configure PBS backup client
   102→- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents
   103→
   104→#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS
   105→
   106→```bash
   107→task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
   108→```
   109→
   110→This will:
   111→
   112→- Stop Docker containers
   113→- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
   114→- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
   115→- Start Docker containers
   116→
   117→#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup
   118→
   119→1. Check the app is working at its URL
   120→1. Verify data is restored correctly
   121→1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:
   122→
   123→```bash
   124→# Compare resource lists between old and new state (no output = match)
   125→diff <(task tofu:state APP=<APP>) <(task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
   126→```
   127→
   128→1. Clean up old state file:
   129→
   130→```bash
   131→rm terraform.tfstate.old
   132→```
   133→
   134→#### Example: Recovering n8n
   135→
   136→```bash
   137→cd tofu/apps/n8n
   138→
   139→# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
   140→IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
   141→ssh-keygen -R $IP
   142→mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
   143→
   144→# 2. Recreate
   145→task tofu:init APP=n8n
   146→task tofu:apply APP=n8n
   147→
   148→# 3. Restore data
   149→task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n
   150→
   151→# 4. Verify app is working
   152→curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
   153→# Should return: {"status":"ok"}
   154→
   155→# 5. Verify state matches (no output = success)
   156→diff <(task tofu:state APP=n8n) <(task tofu:state APP=n8n -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
   157→
   158→# 6. Cleanup
   159→rm terraform.tfstate.old
   160→```
   161→
   162→### Database Recovery
   163→
   164→#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)
   165→
   166→```bash
   167→# 1. List available dumps
   168→ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"
   169→
   170→# 2. Restore using task
   171→task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
   172→```
   173→
   174→#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)
   175→
   176→```bash
   177→# 1. Copy dump to container
   178→ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"
   179→
   180→# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
   181→ssh root@10.100.4.101
   182→
   183→# 3. Restore
   184→docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
   185→```
   186→
   187→#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)
   188→
   189→```bash
   190→# Copy from backup dump directory to container
   191→ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"
   192→
   193→# Restart the service
   194→ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
   195→```
   196→
   197→### Network Services Recovery
   198→
   199→If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.
   200→
   201→1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   202→   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   203→   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)
   204→
   205→2. **Recover AdGuard container**
   206→
   207→   ```bash
   208→   # Check container status
   209→   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"
   210→
   211→   # Start if stopped
   212→   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"
   213→
   214→   # Check AdGuard service
   215→   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   216→   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   217→   ```
   218→
   219→3. **Verify DNS resolution**
   220→
   221→   ```bash
   222→   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   223→   ```
   224→
   225→### Full Host Recovery
   226→
   227→This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.
   228→
   229→#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)
   230→
   231→1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
   232→2. Install to boot drive
   233→3. Configure network:
   234→   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   235→   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   236→   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
   237→4. Import ZFS pool:
   238→
   239→   ```bash
   240→   zpool import tank
   241→   ```
   242→
   243→#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)
   244→
   245→1. Clone the homelab repo:
   246→
   247→   ```bash
   248→   git clone https://github.com/darshan-rambhia/proxmox-homelab.git
   249→   cd homelab
   250→   ```
   251→
   252→2. Sync backup configuration:
   253→
   254→   ```bash
   255→   task backup:sync
   256→   ```
   257→
   258→3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):
   259→
   260→   ```bash
   261→   # List available backups
   262→   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   263→

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

### Stateless Services (No Backup Required)

| ID | Service | Notes |
| -- | ------- | ----- |
| 303 | Immich Importer | Stateless uploader. Auto-starts with Proxmox. No data to backup. |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state (no output = match)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=<APP>) <(task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify app is working
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Verify state matches (no output = success)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=n8n) <(task tofu:state APP=n8n -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)

# 6. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/darshan-rambhia/proxmox-homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2 (offshore backup location):

> **Note:** This procedure has not been fully tested end-to-end. See `proxmox-homelab-vig` for testing task.

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials from 1Password:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Get rclone config from 1Password vault "homelab"
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes with encryption keys
   ```

2. List available backups to verify connectivity:

   ```bash
   rclone ls b2-crypt:vzdump/ --max-depth 1
   rclone ls b2-crypt:database-dumps/ --max-depth 1
   ```

3. Download backups (this may take hours depending on data size):

   ```bash
   # Download vzdump container backups
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/ --progress

   # Download database dumps
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/ --progress
   ```

4. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

### Tier 1: Infrastructure to verify

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working

### Tier 2: Core Services to verify

- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics

### Tier 3: Application Services to verify

- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Jellyfin accessible and library visible (<https://jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] n8n healthcheck passing (`curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz`)
- [ ] Obsidian Sync accessible (<https://obsidian.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Documents (Paperless) accessible (<https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] OpenWebUI accessible (<https://ai.homelab.rambtech.dev>)

### System Health

- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)
- [ ] PBS backup timers active (`task pbs:backup:status APP=<app>`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   ├── 2. PBS (LXC 102) - Backup server (optional but recommended early)
   └── 3. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 4. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 5. Authentik (LXC 203) - SSO/Auth
               └── 6. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

### Stateless Services (No Backup Required)

| ID | Service | Notes |
| -- | ------- | ----- |
| 303 | Immich Importer | Stateless uploader. Auto-starts with Proxmox. No data to backup. |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state (no output = match)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=<APP>) <(task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify app is working
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Verify state matches (no output = success)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=n8n) <(task tofu:state APP=n8n -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)

# 6. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```
