# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "immich_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.immich.container_id
  container_ip   = module.immich.ip_address
  container_name = "immich-docker"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-304"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "PostgreSQL dump"
      command = "docker exec immich_postgres pg_dump -U postgres -d immich --clean --if-exists | gzip > /config/immich-db-backup.sql.gz"
      timeout = 600
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2", "/cache/**"]

    ntfy_priority = "high"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,immich,rotating_light"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["immich"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["immich"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.immich]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cloud Backup - rclone to Backblaze B2
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Generate rclone config from 1Password secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "rclone_conf" {
  filename = "${path.module}/.tmp/rclone.conf"
  content  = <<-CONF
[b2]
type = b2
account = ${local.op.b2_account_id}
key = ${local.op.b2_application_key}
hard_delete = true

[b2-crypt]
type = crypt
remote = b2:rambtech-homelab/photos-encrypted
password = ${local.op.rclone_crypt_password}
password2 = ${local.op.rclone_crypt_password2}
CONF
}

# Install rclone via Ansible
resource "ansible_navigator_run" "install_rclone" {
  depends_on = [module.immich]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = <<-EOT
    - name: Install rclone for cloud backup
      hosts: lxc
      gather_facts: no

      tasks:
        - name: Install required packages
          ansible.builtin.apt:
            name:
              - unzip
              - curl
              - cron
            state: present
            update_cache: yes
            cache_valid_time: 3600

        - name: Check if rclone is installed
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: which rclone
          register: rclone_check
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: false

        - name: Install rclone
          ansible.builtin.shell:
            cmd: curl -fsSL https://rclone.org/install.sh | bash
          when: rclone_check.rc != 0

        - name: Create rclone config directory
          ansible.builtin.file:
            path: /root/.config/rclone
            state: directory
            mode: '0700'
  EOT

  inventory = yamlencode({
    lxc = {
      hosts = {
        "immich" = {
          ansible_host = module.immich.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}

# Deploy rclone config
resource "filesync_file" "rclone_conf" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.rclone_conf.filename
  destination = "/root/.config/rclone/rclone.conf"
  host        = module.immich.ip_address

  mode         = "0600"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [ansible_navigator_run.install_rclone]
}

# Deploy cloud-sync script
resource "filesync_file" "cloud_sync_script" {
  source      = "${path.module}/deploy/cloud-sync.sh"
  destination = "/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh"
  host        = module.immich.ip_address

  mode         = "0755"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [ansible_navigator_run.install_rclone]
}

# Configure cron job for cloud backup
resource "ansible_navigator_run" "configure_cloud_cron" {
  depends_on = [
    filesync_file.cloud_sync_script,
    filesync_file.rclone_conf
  ]

  triggers = {
    container_id   = var.container_id
    cloud_schedule = var.cloud_backup_schedule
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = <<-EOT
    - name: Configure cloud backup cron job
      hosts: lxc
      gather_facts: no
      vars:
        cloud_schedule: "${var.cloud_backup_schedule}"

      tasks:
        - name: Add cloud backup cron job (B2 sync)
          ansible.builtin.cron:
            name: "Cloud backup photos to B2"
            minute: "{{ cloud_schedule.split()[0] }}"
            hour: "{{ cloud_schedule.split()[1] }}"
            day: "{{ cloud_schedule.split()[2] }}"
            month: "{{ cloud_schedule.split()[3] }}"
            weekday: "{{ cloud_schedule.split()[4] }}"
            job: "/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos >> /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log 2>&1"
            user: root

        - name: Ensure cron service is enabled and running
          ansible.builtin.systemd:
            name: cron
            enabled: yes
            state: started

        - name: Display cron configuration
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: "Cloud backup configured: {{ cloud_schedule }}"
  EOT

  inventory = yamlencode({
    lxc = {
      hosts = {
        "immich" = {
          ansible_host = module.immich.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "immich_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "photos"
  backend_url = "http://${module.immich.ip_address}:2283"

  internal_domain = "photos.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "photos.${var.domain_public}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.immich]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.immich.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.immich.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.immich.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.immich_route.internal_url
    public   = module.immich_route.public_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  value = module.immich_route.remote_config_path
}

output "cloud_backup_schedule" {
  description = "Cloud backup cron schedule (to Backblaze B2)"
  value       = var.cloud_backup_schedule
}

# Document Management Stack
# Paperless-ngx (OCR document management) + Stirling-PDF (PDF utilities)

name: documents

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Paperless-ngx - Document Management with OCR
  # ==========================================================================
  # Self-hosted document management with full-text search, auto-tagging,
  # and email consumption. All documents are OCR'd for searchability.
  paperless:
    image: ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:2.20.3
    container_name: paperless
    environment:
      - PAPERLESS_REDIS=redis://paperless-redis:6379
      - PAPERLESS_DBHOST=paperless-db
      - PAPERLESS_DBNAME=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBUSER=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBPASS=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY}
      - PAPERLESS_URL=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev
      # Allow CSRF from both internal and public domains
      - PAPERLESS_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,docs.rambtech.dev,localhost
      - PAPERLESS_CORS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_TIME_ZONE=America/New_York
      - PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE=eng
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_POLLING=60
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_RECURSIVE=true
      - PAPERLESS_TASK_WORKERS=2
      - PAPERLESS_THREADS_PER_WORKER=2
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik (django-allauth)
      - PAPERLESS_APPS=allauth.socialaccount.providers.openid_connect
      - PAPERLESS_SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS=${PAPERLESS_SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS}
      - PAPERLESS_DISABLE_REGULAR_LOGIN=false
      - PAPERLESS_REDIRECT_LOGIN_TO_SSO=false
      - PAPERLESS_SOCIALACCOUNT_ALLOW_SIGNUPS=true
      # Auto-link accounts by email (skip email verification since Authentik already verified)
      - PAPERLESS_ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=none
      - PAPERLESS_SOCIAL_AUTO_SIGNUP=true
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:
      - paperless-data:/usr/src/paperless/data
      - paperless-media:/usr/src/paperless/media
      - ./consume:/usr/src/paperless/consume
      - ./export:/usr/src/paperless/export
    depends_on:
      paperless-db:
        condition: service_healthy
      paperless-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8000/api/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: paperless-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=paperless
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=paperless
    volumes:
      - paperless-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    shm_size: 128mb
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U paperless"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Redis - Cache/Broker for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-redis:
    image: redis:8.4-alpine
    container_name: paperless-redis
    volumes:
      - paperless-redis-data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Stirling-PDF - PDF Manipulation Tools
  # ==========================================================================
  # Comprehensive PDF toolkit: merge, split, compress, OCR, convert, etc.
  # Stateless service - no persistent data needed.
  stirling-pdf:
    image: stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:2.1.5
    container_name: stirling-pdf
    environment:
      - DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false
      - SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=false
      - SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=en_US
      - UI_APPNAME=Stirling PDF
      - UI_HOMEDESCRIPTION=PDF tools for the homelab
      - METRICS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Training data for better OCR (optional)
      - stirling-tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
      # Custom configurations
      - stirling-configs:/configs
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/ | grep -q 'Stirling' || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  paperless-data:
  paperless-media:
  paperless-pgdata:
  paperless-redis-data:
  stirling-tessdata:
  stirling-configs:

from documents.models import Workflow, WorkflowTrigger, WorkflowAction, Tag

# Get existing tags
tags = {t.name.lower(): t for t in Tag.objects.all()}
print(\"Existing tags:\", list(tags.keys()))

# Define folder to tag mappings
# Format: (folder_pattern, tag_name, create_if_missing)
mappings = [
    (\"**/Immigration/**\", \"immigration\", False),
    (\"**/Car/**\", \"car\", False),
    (\"**/Work/**\", \"work\", False),
    (\"**/House*/**\", \"house\", False),
    (\"**/Tax/**\", \"tax\", True),
    (\"**/Kids/**\", \"kids\", True),
    (\"**/medical/**\", \"medical\", True),
    (\"**/books/**\", \"books\", True),
    (\"**/licenses/**\", \"licenses\", True),
    (\"**/passport*/**\", \"immigration\", False),
    (\"**/Darshan*/**\", \"darshan\", False),
    (\"**/Mansi*/**\", \"mansi\", False),
]

created_count = 0
for folder_pattern, tag_name, create_if_missing in mappings:
    # Get or create the tag
    tag = tags.get(tag_name.lower())
    if not tag:
        if create_if_missing:
            tag = Tag.objects.create(name=tag_name)
            tags[tag_name.lower()] = tag
            print(f\"Created tag: {tag_name}\")
        else:
            print(f\"Tag not found, skipping: {tag_name}\")
            continue
    
    # Check if workflow already exists
    workflow_name = f\"Auto-tag: {tag_name} from {folder_pattern}\"
    if Workflow.objects.filter(name=workflow_name).exists():
        print(f\"Workflow already exists: {workflow_name}\")
        continue
    
    # Create workflow
    workflow = Workflow.objects.create(
        name=workflow_name,
        enabled=True,
        order=created_count
    )
    
    # Create trigger
    trigger = WorkflowTrigger.objects.create(
        type=WorkflowTrigger.WorkflowTriggerType.CONSUMPTION,
        filter_path=folder_pattern
    )
    workflow.triggers.add(trigger)
    
    # Create action
    action = WorkflowAction.objects.create(
        type=WorkflowAction.WorkflowActionType.ASSIGNMENT
    )
    action.assign_tags.add(tag)
    workflow.actions.add(action)
    
    print(f\"Created workflow: {workflow_name}\")
    created_count += 1

print(f\"\\nCreated {created_count} workflows\")
"'

docs = Document.objects.all()
tagged_count = 0
already_tagged = 0

for doc in docs:
    original_name = doc.original_filename
    if not original_name:
        continue
    
    # Check if we have folder info for this file
    folders = filename_to_folders.get(original_name, [])
    if not folders:
        continue
    
    # Determine which tags to apply based on folder path
    tags_to_apply = set()
    for folder in folders:
        folder_lower = folder.lower()
        for pattern, tag_name in folder_to_tag.items():
            if pattern in folder_lower:
                if tag_name in tags:
                    tags_to_apply.add(tags[tag_name])
    
    if not tags_to_apply:
        continue
    
    # Check which tags are already applied
    existing_tags = set(doc.tags.all())
    new_tags = tags_to_apply - existing_tags
    
    if new_tags:
        for tag in new_tags:
            doc.tags.add(tag)
        tagged_count += 1
        print(f\"Tagged: {original_name} -> {[t.name for t in new_tags]}\")
    else:
        already_tagged += 1

print(f\"\\nSummary: Tagged {tagged_count} documents, {already_tagged} already had correct tags\")
"'

All 566 documents deleted. 

Regarding your question about **document types and storage paths** best practices in Paperless-ngx:

## Document Types
Best practices:
- **Keep them broad/category-based**: `Invoice`, `Receipt`, `Contract`, `Statement`, `Certificate`, `Form`, `Letter`, `Manual`
- **Don't overlap with tags**: Tags are for *what* it's about (immigration, work), document types are *what kind* of document it is
- **Let Paperless auto-detect**: Enable auto-matching - Paperless learns from your assignments

## Storage Paths
Paperless stores files in a structured way. You can customize the path template:

```
# Default: flat structure with ID
{document_pk}.pdf

# Recommended: organized by year/type
{created_year}/{document_type}/{title}

# Or by correspondent/year
{correspondent}/{created_year}/{title}
```

Common patterns:
- `{created_year}/{correspondent}/{title}` - chronological by sender
- `{document_type}/{created_year}/{title}` - by document type first
- `{tag_list}/{created_year}/{title}` - by tags (can create deep nesting)

You can set the storage path template in **Settings → Storage** or via `PAPERLESS_FILENAME_FORMAT` environment variable.

Great question. Given your use case, here's my recommendation:

## Suggested Approach

**Tags = Use cases / Categories (what you had as folders)**
- `immigration`, `tax`, `work`, `car`, `house`, `medical`, `kids`
- A document can have **multiple tags** (e.g., a passport scan can be tagged `immigration` + `work` + `kids`)
- This replaces the need for duplicating files across folders

**Document Types = What kind of document it is**
- `Certificate` (birth, marriage, degree)
- `Government Form` (I-797, I-140, visa applications)
- `Financial Statement` (bank statements, tax returns, W2s)
- `ID Document` (passport, driver's license, SSN card)
- `Contract/Agreement` (employment offers, leases)
- `Receipt/Invoice`
- `Correspondence` (letters, emails)

## Benefits of This Approach

1. **No more duplicates** - Instead of copying a passport to `Immigration/H1-2015/`, `Immigration/H1-2020/`, and `Work/Onboarding/`, you have ONE passport document tagged with `immigration`, `work`

2. **Better search** - Find all `Government Form` documents, or all documents tagged `immigration` + `tax` (for tax implications of visa status)

3. **Storage path `{created_year}/{title}`** - Clean organization without redundancy

4. **Correspondents** - Use for the *source* (USCIS, IRS, Bank of America, Employer name)

# Document Management Stack
# Paperless-ngx (OCR document management) + Stirling-PDF (PDF utilities)

name: documents

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Paperless-ngx - Document Management with OCR
  # ==========================================================================
  # Self-hosted document management with full-text search, auto-tagging,
  # and email consumption. All documents are OCR'd for searchability.
  paperless:
    image: ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:2.20.3
    container_name: paperless
    environment:
      - PAPERLESS_REDIS=redis://paperless-redis:6379
      - PAPERLESS_DBHOST=paperless-db
      - PAPERLESS_DBNAME=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBUSER=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBPASS=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY}
      - PAPERLESS_URL=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev
      # Allow CSRF from both internal and public domains
      - PAPERLESS_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,docs.rambtech.dev,localhost
      - PAPERLESS_CORS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_TIME_ZONE=America/New_York
      - PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE=eng
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_POLLING=60
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_RECURSIVE=true
      - PAPERLESS_TASK_WORKERS=2
      - PAPERLESS_THREADS_PER_WORKER=2
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik (django-allauth)
      - PAPERLESS_APPS=allauth.socialaccount.providers.openid_connect
      - PAPERLESS_SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS=${PAPERLESS_SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS}
      - PAPERLESS_DISABLE_REGULAR_LOGIN=false
      - PAPERLESS_REDIRECT_LOGIN_TO_SSO=false
      - PAPERLESS_SOCIALACCOUNT_ALLOW_SIGNUPS=true
      # Auto-link accounts by email (skip email verification since Authentik already verified)
      - PAPERLESS_ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=none
      - PAPERLESS_SOCIAL_AUTO_SIGNUP=true
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:
      - paperless-data:/usr/src/paperless/data
      - paperless-media:/usr/src/paperless/media
      - ./consume:/usr/src/paperless/consume
      - ./export:/usr/src/paperless/export
    depends_on:
      paperless-db:
        condition: service_healthy
      paperless-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8000/api/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: paperless-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=paperless
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=paperless
    volumes:
      - paperless-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    shm_size: 128mb
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U paperless"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Redis - Cache/Broker for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-redis:
    image: redis:8.4-alpine
    container_name: paperless-redis
    volumes:
      - paperless-redis-data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Stirling-PDF - PDF Manipulation Tools
  # ==========================================================================
  # Comprehensive PDF toolkit: merge, split, compress, OCR, convert, etc.
  # Stateless service - no persistent data needed.
  stirling-pdf:
    image: stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:2.1.5
    container_name: stirling-pdf
    environment:
      - DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false
      - SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=false
      - SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=en_US
      - UI_APPNAME=Stirling PDF
      - UI_HOMEDESCRIPTION=PDF tools for the homelab
      - METRICS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Training data for better OCR (optional)
      - stirling-tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
      # Custom configurations
      - stirling-configs:/configs
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/ | grep -q 'Stirling' || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  paperless-data:
  paperless-media:
  paperless-pgdata:
  paperless-redis-data:
  stirling-tessdata:
  stirling-configs:

from documents.models import Workflow, WorkflowTrigger, WorkflowAction, DocumentType

# Get document type IDs
doc_types = {dt.name: dt for dt in DocumentType.objects.all()}

# Define document type assignment workflows based on filename patterns
# These use filter_filename with regex patterns
doctype_workflows = [
    # Certificates
    ("DocType: Certificate", "*birth*certificate*|*marriage*certificate*|*degree*|*diploma*", "Certificate", 100),
    
    # Government Forms (immigration forms, visa applications)
    ("DocType: Government Form", "*I-797*|*I-140*|*I-485*|*I-765*|*visa*|*uscis*|*form*", "Government Form", 101),
    
    # Financial Statements
    ("DocType: Financial Statement", "*bank*statement*|*tax*return*|*W2*|*W-2*|*1099*|*pay*stub*|*1040*", "Financial Statement", 102),
    
    # ID Documents
    ("DocType: ID Document", "*passport*|*driver*license*|*ssn*|*social*security*|*state*id*", "ID Document", 103),
    
    # Contracts
    ("DocType: Contract", "*offer*letter*|*employment*|*lease*|*agreement*|*contract*", "Contract", 104),
    
    # Receipts
    ("DocType: Receipt", "*receipt*|*invoice*|*bill*|*payment*", "Receipt", 105),
    
    # Medical Records
    ("DocType: Medical Record", "*medical*|*prescription*|*lab*result*|*health*|*doctor*|*hospital*", "Medical Record", 106),
    
    # Insurance
    ("DocType: Insurance", "*insurance*|*policy*|*claim*|*coverage*", "Insurance", 107),
]

created_workflows = []

for name, pattern, doctype_name, order in doctype_workflows:
    # Check if workflow already exists
    if Workflow.objects.filter(name=name).exists():
        print(f"Workflow '{name}' already exists, skipping")
        continue
    
    doc_type = doc_types.get(doctype_name)
    if not doc_type:
        print(f"Document type '{doctype_name}' not found, skipping {name}")
        continue
    
    # Create workflow
    workflow = Workflow.objects.create(name=name, enabled=True, order=order)
    
    # Create trigger - using CONSUMPTION with filter_filename (glob pattern)
    trigger = WorkflowTrigger.objects.create(
        type=WorkflowTrigger.WorkflowTriggerType.CONSUMPTION,
        filter_filename=pattern
    )
    workflow.triggers.add(trigger)
    
    # Create action - assign document type
    action = WorkflowAction.objects.create(type=WorkflowAction.WorkflowActionType.ASSIGNMENT)
    action.assign_document_type = doc_type
    action.save()
    workflow.actions.add(action)
    
    created_workflows.append(name)
    print(f"Created workflow: {name} -> {doctype_name}")

print(f"\nCreated {len(created_workflows)} document type workflows")
print(f"\nTotal workflows:")
for w in Workflow.objects.all().order_by('order'):
    print(f"  [{w.order}] {w.name} (enabled={w.enabled})")
EOF

Description:
## Overview
Replace current rclone-based Backblaze B2 sync with Proxmox Backup Server's native S3 datastore backend. This eliminates the rclone wrapper layer and integrates B2 directly into PBS.

## Current Architecture

### Backblaze B2 Setup (rclone-based)
- **Method**: Daily rclone sync jobs from Proxmox host
- **Encryption**: rclone crypt layer
- **Storage paths**:
  - `b2-crypt:vzdump` - PBS local backups synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - `b2-crypt:database-dumps` - Database dumps synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - `b2-crypt:` - Photos synced daily at 3:00 AM from LXC 303
- **Configuration**: rclone config in 1Password vault "homelab"

### Current PBS Setup
- **Location**: LXC 102 (10.100.1.102)
- **Local datastore**: Local filesystem
- **Backup targets**: 12 LXC containers (daily/weekly schedules)
- **Pre-backup hooks**: PostgreSQL dumps (Immich, Jellystat), SQLite copies (OpenWebUI, n8n)

## New Architecture (PBS S3 Native)

### PBS S3 Datastore
PBS now supports S3-compatible object stores as native datastores (technology preview feature).

**Benefits**:
- ✅ No rclone wrapper/sync delay
- ✅ Direct backup to cloud (no local-then-sync workflow)
- ✅ PBS handles encryption/deduplication natively
- ✅ Unified backup management in PBS UI
- ✅ Reduced disk I/O on Proxmox host

**Considerations**:
- ⚠️ Technology preview (not production-ready per PBS docs)
- ⚠️ Requires local cache layer (64-128 GB recommended)
- ⚠️ API costs (Backblaze charges for API requests, egress)
- ⚠️ Single PBS instance per S3 datastore (no sharing)
- ⚠️ HTTPS required (no plain HTTP)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Research & Planning

#### 1.1 Backblaze B2 S3 API Research
- [ ] Verify Backblaze B2 S3 API endpoint format
- [ ] Document required credentials format
- [ ] Check B2 pricing for API requests vs download bandwidth
- [ ] Compare costs: current (daily rclone sync) vs native (per-backup API calls)
- [ ] Understand B2 S3 compatibility limitations (if any)

**Backblaze B2 S3 Endpoint Format:**
```
https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com
```
(Region varies by bucket)

#### 1.2 PBS S3 Feature Testing
- [ ] Test PBS S3 datastore creation on test bucket
- [ ] Verify encryption works with S3 backend
- [ ] Test backup/restore cycle
- [ ] Measure cache size requirements for our backup set
- [ ] Test failure scenarios (network loss, API rate limits)

### Phase 2: S3 Endpoint Configuration

**File**: PBS configuration (via CLI on LXC 102)

```bash
# Create S3 endpoint for Backblaze B2
proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create backblaze-b2 \
  --access-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID>' \
  --secret-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY>' \
  --endpoint 's3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com' \
  --region 'us-west-004'
```

**Credentials Source**: 1Password vault "homelab" - rclone B2 config

### Phase 3: S3 Datastore Creation

#### 3.1 Prepare Cache Storage
- [ ] Allocate 128 GB for S3 cache on LXC 102
- [ ] Create filesystem at `/mnt/pbs-s3-cache` or similar
- [ ] Verify disk space available

#### 3.2 Create S3 Datastore
```bash
# Create S3-backed datastore with local cache
proxmox-backup-manager datastore create backblaze-s3 \
  /mnt/pbs-s3-cache \
  --backend type=s3,client=backblaze-b2,bucket=<B2_BUCKET_NAME>
```

### Phase 4: Migration Strategy

**Option A: Parallel Operation (Safer)**
1. Keep existing local PBS datastore + rclone sync
2. Add new S3 datastore alongside
3. Configure NEW backup jobs to use S3 datastore
4. Run both systems in parallel for 30 days
5. Verify S3 backups are reliable
6. Decommission rclone sync jobs
7. Archive old local backups

**Option B: Direct Migration (Riskier)**
1. Stop local backup jobs
2. Create S3 datastore
3. Migrate existing backups to S3 (if possible)
4. Point all jobs to S3 datastore
5. Remove rclone sync

**Recommendation**: Use **Option A** for safety

### Phase 5: Backup Job Updates

Update all PBS backup jobs to target new S3 datastore:
- 12 LXC containers (daily: 304, 501, 502; weekly: 101, 200, 201, 202, 401, 402, 500)
- Keep pre-backup hooks unchanged (database dumps still needed)

### Phase 6: Cost Monitoring

- [ ] Set up Backblaze B2 cost alerts
- [ ] Monitor API request counts
- [ ] Monitor egress bandwidth (if applicable)
- [ ] Compare monthly costs: before (storage + download) vs after (storage + API calls)

### Phase 7: Decommission rclone

After 30 days of verified S3 backups:
- [ ] Disable rclone cron jobs on Proxmox host
- [ ] Archive rclone config to 1Password (keep for recovery)
- [ ] Document S3 datastore configuration for DR
- [ ] Update disaster recovery runbook

## Technical Details

### PBS S3 Datastore Limitations

**From PBS Documentation:**
- Technology preview status (not production-ready)
- No datastore sharing between PBS instances
- HTTPS only (encrypted in transit)
- Requires persistent local filesystem cache (64-128 GB recommended)
- Storage failure handling: cleanup operations may fail if bucket runs out of space

### Cache Sizing Calculation

**Current Backup Set:**
- 12 LXC containers
- Daily backups: 3 containers × 7 days = 21 backups
- Weekly backups: 9 containers × 4 weeks = 36 backups
- Total: ~57 backup snapshots active at any time

**Estimated cache needs:**
- PBS docs recommend 64-128 GB
- Our backup set likely fits in 128 GB cache
- Monitor actual cache usage after deployment

### Cost Comparison

**Current (rclone sync):**
- B2 Storage: $X/month
- B2 Download: $Y/month (for disaster recovery only)
- No API charges (bulk sync)

**Future (PBS S3 native):**
- B2 Storage: $X/month (same)
- B2 API Requests: Class B (write/delete), Class C (read/list)
- B2 Download: Minimal (only cache misses)

**Action**: Calculate expected API request volume before migration

## Testing Checklist

### Pre-Migration Tests (on test bucket)
- [ ] Create test S3 endpoint
- [ ] Create test datastore with S3 backend
- [ ] Run manual backup to S3
- [ ] Verify backup appears in B2 bucket
- [ ] Test restore from S3 backup
- [ ] Simulate network failure during backup
- [ ] Test cache behavior (eviction, refill)

### Post-Migration Tests
- [ ] Verify all 12 containers backup successfully to S3
- [ ] Test restore from S3 datastore
- [ ] Verify pre-backup hooks still execute
- [ ] Check PBS logs for S3 errors
- [ ] Monitor Backblaze B2 dashboard for costs

## Rollback Plan

If S3 datastore proves unreliable:
1. Re-enable local PBS datastore
2. Re-enable rclone sync jobs
3. Keep S3 datastore as secondary/archive
4. Document issues encountered

## Documentation Updates

After successful migration:
- [ ] Update `docs/backups.md` - replace rclone references
- [ ] Update `docs/disaster-recovery.md` - update recovery procedures
- [ ] Update `tasks/cloud.yml` - remove rclone task definitions
- [ ] Document PBS S3 endpoint configuration in runbook
- [ ] Add S3 datastore to PBS monitoring alerts

## References

### PBS S3 Documentation
- PBS Storage S3 Backend: https://pbs.homelab.rambtech.dev/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend
- PBS S3 Endpoint Config: https://pbs.proxmox.com/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend

### Backblaze B2 S3 API
- B2 S3 Compatible API: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html
- B2 S3 Endpoint Regions: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html#regions
- B2 Pricing: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/cloud-storage-pricing.html

### Current Implementation
- Backup strategy: `docs/backups.md`
- Disaster recovery: `docs/disaster-recovery.md`
- Cloud sync scripts: `scripts/backup/cloud-sync.sh`
- rclone config: 1Password vault "homelab"

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| S3 feature instability | High | Use parallel operation (Option A) |
| API cost overrun | Medium | Monitor costs, set alerts |
| Backup failures | High | Keep local backups during transition |
| Cache exhaustion | Medium | Provision 128 GB cache, monitor usage |
| B2 API rate limits | Low | PBS should handle retries |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 12 containers backup successfully to S3 datastore
- [ ] Restore operations work from S3
- [ ] Monthly B2 costs are acceptable (document threshold)
- [ ] No backup failures for 30 consecutive days
- [ ] Cache performance is adequate (no slowdowns)
- [ ] PBS UI shows healthy S3 datastore status

Backblaze B2 has a few options for cost monitoring:

**1. Backblaze Dashboard (Manual)**
- Log into Backblaze B2 console → "Account" → "Billing"
- Shows storage usage, API calls (Class B/C), and download bandwidth
- Can set up email alerts for caps

**2. Backblaze B2 API**
- `b2_get_bucket` returns current storage usage
- No native cost alerting API though

**3. Grafana Cloud Integration**
- Backblaze has an official Grafana Cloud integration
- Shows storage, bandwidth, API calls as metrics

**4. Custom Monitoring via Prometheus**
- Write a simple exporter that queries B2 API for bucket size
- Alert when storage exceeds threshold
- Could run in your monitoring LXC (500)

**5. Simple Approach: Monthly Review**
- B2 is cheap (~$6/TB/month storage, $0.01/10k API calls)
- Just check the dashboard monthly and compare to baseline

Given your homelab setup, the pragmatic options are:
- **Simplest**: Set a B2 "Cap" alert in the Backblaze dashboard (they email you)
- **Integrated**: Add a B2 exporter to your Prometheus stack

Which approach appeals to you? Or would you rather just close this bead and monitor manually for now since B2 costs are typically minimal?
Adding a B2 exporter to the Prometheus stack will incur additional costs right?

content.text:
Yes, it would. The B2 exporter would need to call B2 API periodically to fetch metrics, and Backblaze charges for API calls:

- **Class B** (writes/deletes): $0.004 per 10,000
- **Class C** (reads/lists): $0.004 per 10,000

If the exporter polls every 5 minutes (288 calls/day), that's ~8,640 calls/month = less than $0.01/month. Negligible, but not zero.

The **simplest free option** is just setting a cap alert in the Backblaze dashboard - they'll email you if storage or bandwidth exceeds a threshold you set. No API calls, no cost.

Want me to close this bead with a note to set up the B2 dashboard cap alert manually? That's probably the most sensible approach for a homelab.

content.text:
Based on your homelab (12 LXC containers backing up to PBS → B2, plus photos), here are sensible caps:

| Category | Suggested Cap | Reasoning |
|----------|---------------|-----------|
| **Storage** | $1/day (~165 GB) | Your backups are deduplicated; unlikely to add 165 GB/day. Alerts if something goes wrong. |
| **Download Bandwidth** | $0.50/day (~50 GB) | You only download for disaster recovery. Any significant download = unusual. |
| **Class B Transactions** | $0.10/day (~250k ops) | PBS writes are chunked but deduplicated. Daily backups shouldn't hit this. |
| **Class C Transactions** | $0.10/day (~250k ops) | Read/list ops. Minimal unless restoring. |

**Total daily cap: ~$1.70/day** which would translate to ~$50/month max, but in practice you'll likely see $2-5/month.

For a more conservative approach, you could set everything to **No Cap** except Storage at **$1/day** - that catches runaway backup growth which is the main risk.

proxmox-homelab-45r: Epic: Migrate from Authelia to Authentik
Status: in_progress
Priority: P1
Type: epic
Created: 2025-12-21 00:15
Updated: 2025-12-21 01:16

Description:
Complete migration from Authelia to Authentik as the centralized identity provider.

## Overview
Replace Authelia with Authentik to gain:
- Native Google/GitHub OAuth federation
- OIDC provider capabilities for apps with native SSO support
- Forward auth for apps without native OAuth
- Centralized user/group management
- Jellyfin SSO plugin compatibility

## Phases

### Phase 1: Infrastructure
- Deploy Authentik alongside Traefik in LXC 200
- Configure Google OAuth source
- Setup forward auth middleware in Traefik

### Phase 2: Dashboard & Utility Apps (Forward Auth)
- Homepage, Dashy, Pulse, Arcane, Stirling-PDF
- Prometheus, Alertmanager

### Phase 3: Media & Network Apps (Forward Auth)
- Uptime Kuma, qBittorrent
- Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, SABnzbd
- AdGuard, Traefik Dashboard, ntfy

### Phase 4: Native OIDC Apps
- Grafana, OpenWebUI, Paperless-ngx, n8n, Jellyseerr

### Phase 5: Media Apps (Native OIDC)
- Immich, Jellyfin

### Phase 6: Cleanup
- Decommission Authelia

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All services authenticated via Authentik
- [ ] Google OAuth login working for all users
- [ ] Authelia fully decommissioned
- [ ] All configuration managed as code (OpenTofu/Ansible)

Acceptance Criteria:

    66→## Recovery Procedures
    67→
    68→### Single Container Recovery
    69→
    70→*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
    71→This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.
    72→
    73→#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation
    74→
    75→Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→cd tofu/apps/<APP>
    79→
    80→# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
    81→IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    82→
    83→# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
    84→[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP
    85→
    86→# Rename state to force full recreation
    87→mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
    88→```
    89→
    90→#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure
    91→
    92→```bash
    93→task tofu:init APP=<APP>
    94→task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
    95→```
    96→
    97→This will:
    98→
    99→- Create new LXC container with same VMID
   100→- Run Ansible to configure base system
   101→- Deploy docker-compose and config files
   102→- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
   103→- Configure PBS backup client
   104→- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents
   105→
   106→#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS
   107→
   108→```bash
   109→task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
   110→```
   111→
   112→This will:
   113→
   114→- Stop Docker containers
   115→- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
   116→- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
   117→- Start Docker containers
   118→
   119→#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup
   120→
   121→1. Check the app is working at its URL
   122→1. Verify data is restored correctly
   123→1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:
   124→
   125→```bash
   126→# Compare resource lists between old and new state (no output = match)
   127→diff <(task tofu:state APP=<APP>) <(task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
   128→```
   129→
   130→1. Clean up old state file:
   131→
   132→```bash
   133→rm terraform.tfstate.old
   134→```
   135→
   136→#### Example: Recovering n8n
   137→
   138→```bash
   139→cd tofu/apps/n8n
   140→
   141→# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
   142→IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
   143→ssh-keygen -R $IP
   144→mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
   145→
   146→# 2. Recreate
   147→task tofu:init APP=n8n
   148→task tofu:apply APP=n8n
   149→
   150→# 3. Restore data
   151→task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n
   152→
   153→# 4. Verify app is working
   154→curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
   155→# Should return: {"status":"ok"}
   156→
   157→# 5. Verify state matches (no output = success)
   158→diff <(task tofu:state APP=n8n) <(task tofu:state APP=n8n -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
   159→
   160→# 6. Cleanup
   161→rm terraform.tfstate.old
   162→```
   163→

   229→This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

   233→1. Boot from Proxmox ISO

   246→
   247→1. Clone the homelab repo:

   253→
   254→2. Recreate PBS (LXC 102) first - it's needed for restoring other containers:
   255→
   256→   ```bash
   257→   task tofu:init APP=pbs
   258→   task tofu:apply APP=pbs
   259→   ```
   260→
   261→3. Verify PBS is running and has access to backups:

   273→   task tofu:apply APP=network-services
   274→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=network-services
   275→
   276→   # Traefik
   277→   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   278→   task tofu:apply APP=traefik
   279→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=traefik
   280→
   281→   # Authentik
   282→   task tofu:init APP=authentik
   283→   task tofu:apply APP=authentik
   284→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=authentik
   285→   ```
   286→
   287→#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)
   288→
   289→If the ZFS pool is lost, restore from PBS S3 datastore (Backblaze B2):
   290→
   291→> **Note:** This procedure requires the PBS S3 datastore to be configured. See `proxmox-homelab-vig` for testing task.
   292→
   293→1. Recreate PBS (LXC 102) with fresh state:
   294→
   295→   ```bash
   296→   task tofu:init APP=pbs
   297→   task tofu:apply APP=pbs
   298→   ```
   299→
   300→2. Configure S3 endpoint for Backblaze B2 (get credentials from 1Password):
   301→
   302→   ```bash
   303→   ssh root@10.100.1.102

   305→   # Create S3 endpoint
   306→   proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create backblaze-b2 \
   307→     --access-key '<B2_KEY_ID from 1Password>' \
   308→     --secret-key '<B2_APP_KEY from 1Password>' \
   309→     --endpoint 's3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com' \
   310→     --region 'us-east-005' \
   311→     --path-style true \
   312→     --provider-quirks skip-if-none-match-header
   313→
   314→   # Verify bucket access
   315→   proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint list-buckets backblaze-b2
   316→   ```
   317→
   318→3. Create S3-backed datastore to access cloud backups:
   319→
   320→   ```bash
   321→   # Create cache directory
   322→   mkdir -p /mnt/datastore-s3-cache
   323→
   324→   # Create datastore pointing to B2 bucket
   325→   proxmox-backup-manager datastore create backblaze-s3 /mnt/datastore-s3-cache \
   326→     --backend type=s3,client=backblaze-b2,bucket=rambtech-homelab
   327→   ```
   328→
   329→4. List available backups in S3:
   330→
   331→   ```bash
   332→   proxmox-backup-client list --repository root@pam@localhost:backblaze-s3
   333→   ```
   334→
   335→5. Recreate each container using OpenTofu, then restore data from S3:
   336→
   337→   ```bash
   338→   # For each app (example: n8n)
   339→   task tofu:init APP=n8n
   340→   task tofu:apply APP=n8n
   341→
   342→   # Restore from S3 datastore
   343→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n DATASTORE=backblaze-s3
   344→   ```
   345→
   346→#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)
   347→
   348→1. Start containers in dependency order (if not already running):
   349→
   350→   ```bash
   351→   pct start 102  # PBS
   352→   pct start 101  # Network Services
   353→   pct start 200  # Traefik
   354→   pct start 203  # Authentik

   357→
   358→2. Verify services:

   368→3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:
   369→
   370→   ```bash

   373→   # Review and apply if needed

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   ├── 2. PBS (LXC 102) - Backup server (optional but recommended early)
   └── 3. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 4. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 5. Authentik (LXC 203) - SSO/Auth
               └── 6. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 102 | PBS | 10.100.1.102 | Proxmox | Backup/restore operations |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 203 | Authentik | 10.100.2.203 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authentik |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authentik, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authentik |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authentik |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authentik |

### Stateless Services (No Backup Required)

| ID | Service | Notes |
| -- | ------- | ----- |
| 303 | Immich Importer | Stateless uploader. Auto-starts with Proxmox. No data to backup. |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state (no output = match)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=<APP>) <(task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify app is working
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Verify state matches (no output = success)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=n8n) <(task tofu:state APP=n8n -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)

# 6. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore PBS and Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/darshan-rambhia/proxmox-homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Recreate PBS (LXC 102) first - it's needed for restoring other containers:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=pbs
   task tofu:apply APP=pbs
   ```

3. Verify PBS is running and has access to backups:

   ```bash
   ssh root@10.100.1.102 "proxmox-backup-manager datastore list"
   # Should show 'homelab' and 'backblaze-s3' datastores
   ```

4. Recreate remaining Tier 1 infrastructure using OpenTofu + PBS restore:

   ```bash
   # Network Services
   task tofu:init APP=network-services
   task tofu:apply APP=network-services
   task pbs:backup:restore APP=network-services

   # Traefik
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:apply APP=traefik
   task pbs:backup:restore APP=traefik

   # Authentik
   task tofu:init APP=authentik
   task tofu:apply APP=authentik
   task pbs:backup:restore APP=authentik
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If the ZFS pool is lost, restore from PBS S3 datastore (Backblaze B2):

> **Note:** This procedure requires the PBS S3 datastore to be configured. See `proxmox-homelab-vig` for testing task.

1. Recreate PBS (LXC 102) with fresh state:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=pbs
   task tofu:apply APP=pbs
   ```

2. Configure S3 endpoint for Backblaze B2 (get credentials from 1Password):

   ```bash
   ssh root@10.100.1.102

   # Create S3 endpoint
   proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create backblaze-b2 \
     --access-key '<B2_KEY_ID from 1Password>' \
     --secret-key '<B2_APP_KEY from 1Password>' \
     --endpoint 's3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com' \
     --region 'us-east-005' \
     --path-style true \
     --provider-quirks skip-if-none-match-header

   # Verify bucket access
   proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint list-buckets backblaze-b2
   ```

3. Create S3-backed datastore to access cloud backups:

   ```bash
   # Create cache directory
   mkdir -p /mnt/datastore-s3-cache

   # Create datastore pointing to B2 bucket
   proxmox-backup-manager datastore create backblaze-s3 /mnt/datastore-s3-cache \
     --backend type=s3,client=backblaze-b2,bucket=rambtech-homelab
   ```

4. List available backups in S3:

   ```bash
   proxmox-backup-client list --repository root@pam@localhost:backblaze-s3
   ```

5. Recreate each container using OpenTofu, then restore data from S3:

   ```bash
   # For each app (example: n8n)
   task tofu:init APP=n8n
   task tofu:apply APP=n8n

   # Restore from S3 datastore
   task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n DATASTORE=backblaze-s3
   ```

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order (if not already running):

   ```bash
   pct start 102  # PBS
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 203  # Authentik
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

### Tier 1: Infrastructure to verify

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authentik login working

### Tier 2: Core Services to verify

- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics

### Tier 3: Application Services to verify

- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Jellyfin accessible and library visible (<https://jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] n8n healthcheck passing (`curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz`)
- [ ] Obsidian Sync accessible (<https://obsidian.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Documents (Paperless) accessible (<https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] OpenWebUI accessible (<https://ai.homelab.rambtech.dev>)

### System Health

- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)
- [ ] PBS backup timers active (`task pbs:backup:status APP=<app>`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

## 1Password/Secrets Recovery

All homelab secrets are stored in 1Password under the `homelab` vault. This section documents how to recover access and use secrets during DR scenarios.

### Prerequisites

- 1Password account with access to `homelab` vault
- 1Password CLI (`op`) v2.23.0+ installed
- Biometric authentication configured (or master password)

### 1Password Vault Contents

| Item | Purpose | Used By |
| ---- | ------- | ------- |
| `opentofu` | State encryption passphrase, Proxmox API token | OpenTofu state, Proxmox provider |
| `Cloudflare` | API tokens, tunnel token | DNS, Cloudflare tunnel |
| `grafana` | Admin password | Grafana dashboard |
| `discord-alertmanager-webhook` | Webhook URL | Alertmanager notifications |
| `uptime-kuma` | Admin credentials | Uptime Kuma login |
| `alloy-telemetry` | Push auth credentials | Loki/Prometheus ingestion |
| `authentik` | Admin creds, secret key, Google OAuth, Postgres password | Authentik IdP |
| `Backblaze` | B2 account ID, application key | PBS S3 datastore |
| `backblaze-rclone-crypt` | Encryption passwords (obscured) | rclone crypt layer |
| `pulse` | Admin credentials | Pulse container management |
| `arcane` | Encryption key, JWT secret | Arcane container updates |
| `pulse-agents` | Per-LXC agent tokens (sections) | Pulse agents on each LXC |
| `arcane-agents` | Per-LXC bootstrap tokens (sections) | Arcane agents on each LXC |
| `paperless` | Admin password, secret key, DB password | Paperless-ngx |
| `pbs-backup-user` | PBS backup user password | PBS client authentication |

### Recovery Procedure

#### Step 1: Install 1Password CLI

```bash
# macOS
brew install 1password-cli

# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)
curl -sS https://downloads.1password.com/linux/keys/1password.asc | \
  sudo gpg --dearmor --output /usr/share/keyrings/1password-archive-keyring.gpg
echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/1password-archive-keyring.gpg] https://downloads.1password.com/linux/debian/$(dpkg --print-architecture) stable main" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/1password.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install 1password-cli
```

#### Step 2: Sign In to 1Password

```bash
# Interactive sign-in (will prompt for master password or biometric)
eval $(op signin)

# Verify access to homelab vault
op vault list | grep homelab
```

#### Step 3: Retrieve Specific Secrets

```bash
# State encryption passphrase (needed for tofu init)
op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"

# Proxmox API token
op read "op://homelab/opentofu/proxmox_api_token"

# Backblaze B2 credentials (for PBS S3)
op read "op://homelab/Backblaze/keyId"
op read "op://homelab/Backblaze/b2_app_key"

# Authentik secret key
op read "op://homelab/authentik/secret_key"
```

#### Step 4: Export for Offline Use (Emergency Only)

In case 1Password becomes inaccessible during a DR event, you can export critical secrets:

```bash
# Export homelab vault to encrypted file (store securely!)
op document create --vault homelab --title "DR-Export-$(date +%Y%m%d)" \
  <(op item list --vault homelab --format json | op item get - --format json)

# Alternative: Export specific items to environment file
cat > /tmp/dr-secrets.env << EOF
TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase=$(op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password")
PROXMOX_VE_API_TOKEN=$(op read "op://homelab/opentofu/proxmox_api_token")
B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID=$(op read "op://homelab/Backblaze/keyId")
B2_APPLICATION_KEY=$(op read "op://homelab/Backblaze/b2_app_key")
EOF

# Use the exported secrets
source /tmp/dr-secrets.env
task tofu:apply APP=network-services

# CRITICAL: Delete after use!
rm /tmp/dr-secrets.env
```

### OpenTofu Integration

The homelab uses 1Password as the secrets backend for OpenTofu. During normal operations:

1. Secrets are fetched at plan/apply time via the 1Password provider
2. The `TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase` is set by Taskfile from 1Password
3. All other secrets are accessed via `local.op.<secret_name>` in Terraform code

If 1Password is unavailable:

1. Use the exported secrets from Step 4 above
2. Set `TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase` manually
3. OpenTofu will fail on 1Password data sources - you'll need to temporarily hardcode values or use `-target` to skip

### Recovery Without 1Password Access

If you've lost access to 1Password entirely:

1. **Proxmox root access** - Use local root password (physical access to server)
2. **Container access** - SSH keys are in the repo, containers use key-based auth
3. **Service passwords** - Most can be reset via container CLI:
   ```bash
   # Reset Grafana admin password
   docker exec grafana grafana-cli admin reset-admin-password <new-password>

   # Reset Authentik admin password
   docker exec authentik-server ak create_admin_user
   ```
4. **Database passwords** - Recreate containers with new passwords, restore data from backups
5. **Cloudflare/B2** - Contact support with account recovery, or recreate from scratch

---

## Rollback Procedure for Failed Recovery

If a container recovery fails partway through, use these procedures to rollback and retry.

### Symptoms of Failed Recovery

- `tofu apply` fails mid-execution
- Container starts but services don't come up
- PBS restore fails or restores corrupted data
- State file is out of sync with actual infrastructure

### Rollback Scenarios

#### Scenario 1: OpenTofu Apply Failed Mid-Execution

The container may exist but be partially configured.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Check what state thinks exists
tofu state list

# Check actual container status on Proxmox
ssh root@homelab "pct status <CONTAINER_ID>"

# Option A: Destroy and recreate
tofu destroy -auto-approve
rm terraform.tfstate.old  # if exists
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>

# Option B: Import existing container into state (if container is running fine)
tofu import 'module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc' <CONTAINER_ID>
task tofu:plan APP=<APP>  # Review what changes are needed
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

#### Scenario 2: PBS Restore Failed

Data restore didn't complete or restored corrupted data.

```bash
# 1. Check what backups are available
task pbs:backup:list APP=<APP>

# 2. Stop containers to prevent further data corruption
ssh root@<CONTAINER_IP> "cd /config && docker compose down"

# 3. Clear the failed restore (remove partially restored data)
ssh root@<CONTAINER_IP> "rm -rf /config/*"

# 4. Re-run OpenTofu to redeploy fresh configs
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>

# 5. Restore from a different snapshot
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP> SNAPSHOT=<older-snapshot-id>

# 6. If all PBS backups are corrupted, restore from B2 (if available)
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP> DATASTORE=backblaze-s3
```

#### Scenario 3: Container Won't Start After Restore

The container exists but fails to start or services crash.

```bash
# 1. Check container logs
ssh root@homelab "pct enter <CONTAINER_ID>"
journalctl -xe

# 2. Check Docker container logs
ssh root@<CONTAINER_IP> "docker logs <container-name>"

# 3. Common fixes:
#    - Permission issues: chown -R root:root /config
#    - Docker socket: systemctl restart docker
#    - Disk full: df -h && docker system prune -af

# 4. Nuclear option: destroy and full recreate
cd tofu/apps/<APP>
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.failed
ssh root@homelab "pct destroy <CONTAINER_ID> --force"
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

#### Scenario 4: State File Corruption

OpenTofu state is corrupted or out of sync.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# 1. Backup corrupted state
cp terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.corrupted

# 2. Check if we have state backup
ls -la terraform.tfstate.backup terraform.tfstate.old 2>/dev/null

# 3. Option A: Restore from backup
cp terraform.tfstate.backup terraform.tfstate
task tofu:plan APP=<APP>

# 3. Option B: Fresh start (destroy existing container first!)
ssh root@homelab "pct destroy <CONTAINER_ID> --force"
rm terraform.tfstate*
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

### Rollback Checklist

After any rollback, verify:

- [ ] Container is running: `pct status <ID>`
- [ ] Docker containers are up: `docker ps`
- [ ] Service responds: `curl http://<IP>:<PORT>/health`
- [ ] State matches reality: `tofu plan` shows no changes
- [ ] Backups are scheduled: `task pbs:backup:status APP=<APP>`

### Prevention

To avoid needing rollbacks:

1. **Always run `tofu plan` before `apply`** - Review changes before executing
2. **Keep old state files** - Rename to `.old` instead of deleting until verified
3. **Test restores regularly** - Monthly test restore to catch backup issues early
4. **Check PBS backup status** - Ensure backups completed before attempting restore

---

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

    16→## Service Dependencies
    17→

    30→
    31→### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)
    32→
    33→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
    34→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
    35→| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
    36→| 102 | PBS | 10.100.1.102 | Proxmox | Backup/restore operations |
    37→| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
    38→| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |

    41→### Tier 2: Core Services

    44→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
    45→| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
    46→| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |
    47→
    48→### Tier 3: Application Services
    49→
    50→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
    51→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
    52→| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authentik |
    53→| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |

    65→
    66→## Recovery Procedures
    67→
    68→### Single Container Recovery
    69→
    70→*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
    71→This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.
    72→
    73→#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation
    74→
    75→Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→cd tofu/apps/<APP>
    79→
    80→# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
    81→IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

    83→# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
    84→[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP
    85→
    86→# Rename state to force full recreation
    87→mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
    88→```
    89→
    90→#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure
    91→
    92→```bash
    93→task tofu:init APP=<APP>
    94→task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
    95→```
    96→
    97→This will:
    98→
    99→- Create new LXC container with same VMID
   100→- Run Ansible to configure base system
   101→- Deploy docker-compose and config files
   102→- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
   103→- Configure PBS backup client
   104→- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents
   105→
   106→#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS
   107→
   108→```bash
   109→task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
   110→```
   111→
   112→This will:
   113→
   114→- Stop Docker containers
   115→- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
   116→- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
   117→- Start Docker containers
   118→
   119→#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup
   120→
   121→1. Check the app is working at its URL
   122→1. Verify data is restored correctly
   123→1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:
   124→
   125→```bash
   126→# Compare resource lists between old and new state (no output = match)
   127→diff <(task tofu:state APP=<APP>) <(task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
   128→```
   129→
   130→1. Clean up old state file:
   131→
   132→```bash
   133→rm terraform.tfstate.old
   134→```
   135→
   136→#### Example: Recovering n8n
   137→
   138→```bash
   139→cd tofu/apps/n8n
   140→
   141→# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
   142→IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
   143→ssh-keygen -R $IP
   144→mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
   145→
   146→# 2. Recreate
   147→task tofu:init APP=n8n
   148→task tofu:apply APP=n8n
   149→
   150→# 3. Restore data
   151→task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n
   152→
   153→# 4. Verify app is working
   154→curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
   155→# Should return: {"status":"ok"}
   156→
   157→# 5. Verify state matches (no output = success)
   158→diff <(task tofu:state APP=n8n) <(task tofu:state APP=n8n -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
   159→
   160→# 6. Cleanup
   161→rm terraform.tfstate.old
   162→```
   163→

   165→
   166→#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

   174→```
   175→
   176→#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

   179→# 1. Copy dump to container

   181→
   182→# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
   183→ssh root@10.100.4.101

   189→#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

   194→
   195→# Restart the service
   196→ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
   197→```
   198→
   199→### Network Services Recovery
   200→
   201→If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.
   202→
   203→1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   204→   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   205→   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)
   206→
   207→2. **Recover AdGuard container**
   208→
   209→   ```bash
   210→   # Check container status
   211→   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"
   212→
   213→   # Start if stopped
   214→   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"
   215→
   216→   # Check AdGuard service
   217→   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   218→   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   219→   ```
   220→
   221→3. **Verify DNS resolution**
   222→
   223→   ```bash
   224→   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   225→   ```
   226→
   227→### Full Host Recovery
   228→
   229→This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.
   230→
   231→#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)
   232→
   233→1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
   234→2. Install to boot drive
   235→3. Configure network:
   236→   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   237→   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   238→   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
   239→4. Import ZFS pool:
   240→
   241→   ```bash
   242→   zpool import tank
   243→   ```
   244→
   245→#### Phase 2: Restore PBS and Configuration (30 min)
   246→
   247→1. Clone the homelab repo:
   248→
   249→   ```bash
   250→   git clone https://github.com/darshan-rambhia/proxmox-homelab.git
   251→   cd homelab
   252→   ```
   253→
   254→2. Recreate PBS (LXC 102) first - it's needed for restoring other containers:
   255→
   256→   ```bash
   257→   task tofu:init APP=pbs
   258→   task tofu:apply APP=pbs
   259→   ```
   260→
   261→3. Verify PBS is running and has access to backups:
   262→
   263→   ```bash
   264→   ssh root@10.100.1.102 "proxmox-backup-manager datastore list"
   265→   # Should show 'homelab' and 'backblaze-s3' datastores
   266→   ```
   267→
   268→4. Recreate remaining Tier 1 infrastructure using OpenTofu + PBS restore:
   269→
   270→   ```bash
   271→   # Network Services
   272→   task tofu:init APP=network-services
   273→   task tofu:apply APP=network-services
   274→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=network-services
   275→
   276→   # Traefik
   277→   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   278→   task tofu:apply APP=traefik
   279→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=traefik
   280→
   281→   # Authentik
   282→   task tofu:init APP=authentik
   283→   task tofu:apply APP=authentik
   284→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=authentik
   285→   ```
   286→
   287→#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)
   288→
   289→If the ZFS pool is lost, restore from PBS S3 datastore (Backblaze B2):
   290→
   291→> **Note:** This procedure requires the PBS S3 datastore to be configured. See `proxmox-homelab-vig` for testing task.
   292→
   293→1. Recreate PBS (LXC 102) with fresh state:
   294→
   295→   ```bash
   296→   task tofu:init APP=pbs
   297→   task tofu:apply APP=pbs
   298→   ```
   299→
   300→2. Configure S3 endpoint for Backblaze B2 (get credentials from 1Password):
   301→
   302→   ```bash
   303→   ssh root@10.100.1.102
   304→
   305→   # Create S3 endpoint
   306→   proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create backblaze-b2 \
   307→     --access-key '<B2_KEY_ID from 1Password>' \
   308→     --secret-key '<B2_APP_KEY from 1Password>' \
   309→     --endpoint 's3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com' \
   310→     --region 'us-east-005' \
   311→     --path-style true \
   312→     --provider-quirks skip-if-none-match-header
   313→
   314→   # Verify bucket access
   315→   proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint list-buckets backblaze-b2
   316→   ```
   317→
   318→3. Create S3-backed datastore to access cloud backups:
   319→
   320→   ```bash
   321→   # Create cache directory
   322→   mkdir -p /mnt/datastore-s3-cache
   323→
   324→   # Create datastore pointing to B2 bucket
   325→   proxmox-backup-manager datastore create backblaze-s3 /mnt/datastore-s3-cache \
   326→     --backend type=s3,client=backblaze-b2,bucket=rambtech-homelab
   327→   ```
   328→
   329→4. List available backups in S3:
   330→
   331→   ```bash
   332→   proxmox-backup-client list --repository root@pam@localhost:backblaze-s3
   333→   ```
   334→
   335→5. Recreate each container using OpenTofu, then restore data from S3:
   336→
   337→   ```bash
   338→   # For each app (example: n8n)
   339→   task tofu:init APP=n8n
   340→   task tofu:apply APP=n8n
   341→
   342→   # Restore from S3 datastore
   343→   task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n DATASTORE=backblaze-s3
   344→   ```
   345→
   346→#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)
   347→
   348→1. Start containers in dependency order (if not already running):
   349→
   350→   ```bash
   351→   pct start 102  # PBS
   352→   pct start 101  # Network Services
   353→   pct start 200  # Traefik
   354→   pct start 203  # Authentik
   355→   # ... rest of containers
   356→   ```
   357→
   358→2. Verify services:
   359→
   360→   ```bash
   361→   # DNS
   362→   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   363→
   364→   # Web services
   365→   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   366→   ```
   367→
   368→3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:
   369→
   370→   ```bash
   371→   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   372→   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   373→   # Review and apply if needed
   374→   ```
   375→
   376→## Verification Checklist
   377→
   378→After any recovery, verify:
   379→
   380→### Tier 1: Infrastructure to verify
   381→
   382→- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
   383→- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
   384→- [ ] Authentik login working
   385→
   386→### Tier 2: Core Services to verify
   387→
   388→- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
   389→- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
   390→
   391→### Tier 3: Application Services to verify
   392→
   393→- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
   394→- [ ] Jellyfin accessible and library visible (<https://jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
   395→- [ ] n8n healthcheck passing (`curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz`)
   396→- [ ] Obsidian Sync accessible (<https://obsidian.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
   397→- [ ] Documents (Paperless) accessible (<https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
   398→- [ ] OpenWebUI accessible (<https://ai.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
   399→
   400→### System Health
   401→
   402→- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)
   403→- [ ] PBS backup timers active (`task pbs:backup:status APP=<app>`)
   404→
   405→## Preventive Measures
   406→
   407→### Regular Testing
   408→
   409→- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
   410→- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time
   411→
   412→### Monitoring Gaps to Address
   413→
   414→- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
   415→- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)
   416→
   417→## Contact & Escalation
   418→
   419→For issues beyond this runbook:
   420→
   421→- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
   422→- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>
   423→
